## November 26, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: falling damage and Hero knockout recovery

### Falling damage

For current HP/d20 play, an uncontrolled fall of H feet deals `min(1500, 3 × max(0, H − 10))` HP damage: the first 10 ft are safe, each additional foot deals 3 HP, and the terminal-velocity cap is 1,500 HP (reached at 510 ft). Landing in sufficiently deep water subtracts 100 damage after the cap, to a minimum of zero. Ordinary Armor Rating and Energy Resistance do not mitigate falling damage; falling cannot critically hit. Ordinary Evasion or a generic saving throw does not negate an unavoidable impact. Heavy equipment does not independently multiply this damage. A controlled descent need not be an uncontrolled fall.

Fall recovery is ordinarily a defensive action. The falling character or an ally can prepare a specific lawful defense to arrest, catch or cushion the fall, respecting normal action/preparation timing, Channel Limit, MP, range, medium, equipment, actual anchors and capacity. Examples include flight, a tractor beam, catching threads, controlled water or a genuine handhold; applicable Technique may resolve a legitimate grab or maneuver, not a generic damage reduction. No free reaction or new casting permission. Sufficiently cushioning surfaces can reduce the effective uncontrolled falling distance; exact other surface modifiers and defense effectiveness remain GM adjudication. An unconscious character in water may drown; the impact's survival protection does not prevent subsequent drowning.

### Fall-induced emergency Shimmer Break

Apply eligible fall prevention and water reduction before testing the impact. An intact, dormant Hero Shimmer Guard breaks under the ordinary emergency threshold or when the remaining falling damage equals or exceeds maximum ordinary HP (fall-specific exception closing the ordinary threshold gap). The otherwise catastrophic impact does not kill the Hero; instead set ordinary HP to **0**, forfeit the entire Shimmer Reserve, break the Guard, and leave the Hero prone, unconscious and helpless. This replaces the ordinary emergency Break's retention of pre-impact HP only for falling. A Guard already active or broken cannot perform this emergency Break; otherwise retain ordinary lawful damage routing and existing Shimmer recovery. No automatic protection against subsequent hazards.

### Hero knockout and recovery

Track a single HP-related knockout count since the last qualifying long rest. Ordinary HP-related defeat (after applicable Shimmer protection, not merely ordinary HP reaching zero while reserve still protects the Hero) and fall-induced Shimmer Break share this count. Ordinary emergency Break without incapacitation does not count. Magical Sleep and other distinct incapacitating conditions retain their own rules.

| Rule | First knockout since long rest | Second and subsequent knockouts before long rest |
|---|---|---|
| Unconsciousness duration | 1 hour | 8 hours |
| Early awakening | Heal ordinary HP to at least ceil(25% of maximum ordinary HP) | None, even if fully healed |
| Natural awakening, if alive | At least ceil(10% of maximum ordinary HP) | At least ceil(10% of maximum ordinary HP) |

Knocked-out Heroes cannot act or defend and may receive healing. Partial healing below the first-knockout wake threshold is retained but does not wake them. On natural awakening, set ordinary HP to the greater of current HP and ceil(10% of maximum ordinary HP), without lowering existing healing or exceeding maximum HP. The first knockout may end early when the threshold is reached; a repeated knockout lasts the full eight hours. Completing a qualifying long rest resets the count; involuntary unconsciousness itself does not count as restorative sleep, reset the counter, restore Shimmer, or grant ordinary sleep-based MP or HP recovery beyond the specified awakening floor. Ordinary Shimmer recovery timing remains independent.

Preserve other current HP/d20 damage, healing, status and Shimmer rules. Drowning, execution, general death rules for unconscious Heroes, normal reserve overflow details, precise other cushioning modifiers and final quantitative balance remain unresolved. The fixed damage cap is an approved gameplay benchmark, not a physics calculation or simulation result. No historical engine or saved character migration.

Affected: Combat, World and Shimmer, Magical Media and Contests, Canon Index, and public health/combat guides. The falling-specific Break and explicit HP knockout recovery supersede earlier open hazard and incapacitation notes to this extent only. Public health examples corrected to the already-approved 115 natural HP constant. No simulation or character manager update.

## November 26, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: Mana Capacity training

Current HP/d20 Heroes may purchase **Mana Capacity** with Training Points from level 1, without an END prerequisite or percentage-based purchase cap. Each purchased rank grants a flat **+5 maximum MP**, up to 20 ranks / **+100 MP**. The price belongs to the next rank; keep TP and purchased ranks in the ordinary training ledger.

| Purchased rank | TP per rank | Cumulative TP at end of band | Total trained MP at end of band |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1–5 | 2 | 10 | +25 |
| 6–10 | 3 | 25 | +50 |
| 11–15 | 4 | 45 | +75 |
| 16–20 | 5 | 70 | +100 |

Add the flat trained capacity **after** the existing +10 natural-MP compensation and applicable racial capacity calculation/multipliers. The same added capacity supports Soul Strain: it is one shared reservoir, not a separate free strain pool. Existing strain deductions, racial equipment-strain limitations, affinities, lawful use and recovery rules remain. Moontouched receive the trained increase for Soul Strain capacity only; their usable natural MP remains zero. Drakyn retain feeding-only recovery by consuming Starspawn. Thornguard retain their casting restrictions and existing equipment-strain ceiling. Mana Capacity does not increase END, HP, Channel Limit, spell damage, Leywell capacity, or change recovery methods. Enchanted END still cannot increase MP/strain capacity; cybernetic END retains its existing distinct effects. This is an independent training route for INT, Skill and martial builds, not a new source of spell access. No simulation or implementation change is implied.

Affected: World and Shimmer, Combat, Equipment, Canon Index and public player training, character and enchantment guides. Supersedes the absence of an independent mana capacity purchase; no other training price changes, simulation or character manager migration. Balance remains untested.

## November 26, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: refined Skill training progression and HP allowance

For current HP/d20 Heroes at level L, let S be the number of actually allocated base attribute points invested in Skill. Baseline TP remains 2L; total ordinary earned TP = floor(2L + S × t(L)). Skill SP income remains +2 SP per allocated Skill point (ordinary earned SP = 2L + 2S); the former one-to-one SP/TP income relationship and flat +2 TP per Skill are superseded for this progression. Racial starting Skill, racial multipliers, automatic fifth-level increases, enchantments and implants do not count as S. Preserve independently approved exceptional grants, separate ledgers and existing purchase costs.

| Level | TP per invested Skill t | Additional purchased HP allowance per invested Skill k |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1–10 | 0.5 | 0 |
| 25 | 1 | 0 |
| 50 | 2 | 1 |
| 75 | 2.5 | 1 |
| 100 | 2.5 | 1.5 |

Linearly interpolate between anchors, recalculate at current level, and floor the final TP budget once. Purchased HP ceiling = floor(1.5 × natural HP + k(L) × S). Effective purchased HP is limited to this ceiling; actual HP ranks must still be bought with TP. HP training remains available from level 1, and its per-rank benefit and cost are not changed here. Skill grants no free HP or natural HP. Preserve racial/augmentation exclusions and existing Shimmer rules. No automatic refund or reset of saved ledgers.

Validation: Combat Lab job ba931a10-36bd-49b1-882e-650a00000011, 297,000 encounters, 220 constructions and 990 matchup checks passed. Five Skill investment shares and eleven levels tested under both AR policies. Strong AR remains experimental, not approved here; caster balance and armor specialist spending remain open. Stationary duels, permissive equipment and fixed strategies limit conclusions. Historical engines unchanged.

## November 26, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: level-one point budgets

In the current HP/d20 Hero game, a newly created level-1 Hero receives **2 allocatable base attribute (stat) points, 2 Skill Points (SP), and 2 Training Points (TP)**, in addition to the racial starting array and existing exceptional grants. These are separate pools, available before purchases. Each subsequent level continues the existing +2 attribute points and +2 SP/+2 TP income; the existing +1 to all five base attributes every fifth level remains unchanged. Baseline earned totals at level L are 2L attribute points, 2L SP and 2L TP (including the starting grant), with no second level-one award. Each actually allocated Skill attribute point grants +2 SP and +2 TP; racial base Skill, racial modifiers and automatic fifth-level increases do not count. Record earned, spent and unspent balances separately. This is not a new universal non-Hero advancement rule or automatic refund/reset of saved character ledgers.

Apply the +10 compensation to ordinary natural capacity before existing racial capacity multipliers, retaining Soul Strain and affinity rules. Moontouched usable natural MP remains hard-capped at zero, but the +10 is included in Soul Strain capacity accounting. Drakyn have a natural maximum MP and recover only by consuming Starspawn, never by resting.

For the developing HP/d20 modular Channel Limit, use floor(1 + governing effective attribute/10 + applicable Craft Mastery), preserving existing Craft-specific modifiers, nominal investment, action and resource constraints. Warlocks retain INT or END governing choice and half ordinary throughput; apply the +1 compensation before the specialty multiplier, with final downward rounding. This approval does not resolve unspecified Mastery accrual.

For the practical noncombat waist-height lift benchmark, pounds = 100 × (max(0,effective STR+10)/15)^2. Restore the removed offset in other legacy noncombat benchmarks dependent on that old scale, not in separately compensated combat equations; exact other benchmark conversions remain open.

Approved HP/d20 rebase compensation: natural HP max(1,floor(115 + marginal END)), marginal bands 4 per point through 50, 3.5 through 100, 3 above, extending the first band linearly to −10. Conventional STR-derived contribution 10 + marginal STR (1 through 50, 1.5 through 100, 2 above; extend to −10), Hulking doubles that contribution, and INT-derived magical contribution uses the same marginal curve plus 10. Preserve other damage sources and final nonnegative damage. Shared equipped capacity max(0,floor(20+effective STR+effective END)). Accuracy/evasion formulas unchanged. Retain existing training, racial exceptions and Shimmer rules. Historical engines unchanged.

Deterministic melee gate audit (not a new equipment approval): 13 playable races × 31 shapes × levels 1/5/10 × four policies = 4,836 comparisons. QI Boughsteel, no equipment bonuses; later levels allocate all earned points evenly to STR/DEX and apply five-level increments. Existing gate pass totals 80/194/271 of 403 per level; subtract 10 from each gate, minimum 1: 262/321/361; remove Light gates after rebase: identical; remove ordinary Light/Medium gates after rebase: 272/321/361. Existing level-1 gates exclude Moontouched, Bloomkin, Corvyn, Kobold from every melee profile. Rebased gates permit all 13 races all eight Light shapes. Weight-first is recommended, not yet approved; actual individual HP/d20 Weight catalogue, Honed early requirements, armor and shield loadout profiles remain unresolved. No combat trials. ## November 25, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: inoculation development and prevalence

Cumulative qualifying comfortable exposure benchmarks for adults to reach inoculation I/II/III/IV/V are 7 days / 3 months / 1 year / 5 years / 15 years. Children adapt twice as fast (approximately 3–4 days / 6 weeks / 6 months / 2.5 years / 7.5 years under continuous childhood conditions). Qualifying stress multipliers: negligible 0, comfortable sustained 1, persistent mild sickness 2, moderate sickness 3, severe chronic sickness 4; acute poisoning is a medical crisis, not reliable accelerated adaptation. Childhood and stress multipliers combine. These are cumulative exposure benchmarks, not automatic aging or guaranteed progression; equilibrium can halt advancement, and excessive burden can cause crisis before adaptation. Exact stress/burden boundaries and clock implementation remain open.

Infants temporarily retain maternal environmental absorption protection, not permanent inoculation or its penalties; protection fades in the first few months. Sheltered newborns, filtered infant environments, gradual childhood exposure and protected nurseries/schools are typical adaptation practices where needed, not compulsory rites. Preserve latest social-class distinctions and protected wealthy households. Illustrative ordinary Scarlands settlement adult inoculation distribution 0/I/II/III/IV/V = 5/10/20/45/17/3 percent; not a universal census or simulated population. Tier V is uncommon, concentrated among long-exposed workers, disaster survivors and other high-risk groups. At reference END 10, Tier III reaches daily equilibrium in continuous Haze II; continuous Haze III exceeds capacity even at Tier V. Ordinary mask and circle protection remains nonstacking. 

## November 25, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: Scarlander inoculation and social class

Inoculation is a biological compromise, not a universal cultural rite. Wealthy households can often avoid it through filtered neighborhoods and high-end Clearbreaths when traversing toxic environments. The richest Blood Courts normally remain uninoculated unless specific military, industrial, alchemical, frontier or security needs justify adaptation. Middle-class families make the clearest deliberate tradeoff, sometimes choosing light childhood inoculation and then protected living, depending on hometown Haze and infrastructure. Poor residents and exposed workers often have little choice. Illustrative tendencies, not mandatory class restrictions: great courts 0, wealthy 0–I, upper middle 0–II, middle I–III, working poor II–IV, chronically exposed laborers III–V. Uninoculated old age can mark privilege. Local prevalence depends on wealth, infrastructure and occupation; no universal population distribution. Preserve temporary maternal protection, faster childhood adaptation and existing permanent penalties; exact adaptation schedules, child/stress multipliers and maternal protection magnitude remain open.

## November 25, 2026 — AUTHOR RULING: Hex exposure, medical crisis and treatment

In the current HP/d20 game, Hexed I triggers at 1× applicable status threshold and Hexed II at 2×; acute Hex Sickness at 4× and Hex-induced coma at 8×. This supersedes older Hex-specific 4× Severity II references for the current game; preserve historical rulesets. Use the current effective status HP basis (ordinary current HP, Hero floor of 25% ordinary maximum HP), not the old independent resistance statistic, subject to future named Hex resistance modifiers. Preserve legal application and counterplay. Medical crisis persistence/recovery details remain open; ordinary status clearing does not imply reversal of established mutation.

Ordinary isolated exposure below 50% of applicable threshold is generally exempt from chronic bookkeeping. DM should account for recurrent near-threshold exposure, particularly daily incidents. Gradual prolonged bodily exposure can produce permanent inoculation with Hex resistance benefits at costs to health, mana output and lifespan. END governs physiological tolerance. Acute exposure and chronic accumulation can both arise from ambient Haze, hostile Hex delivery, gadget emissions/rapid refueling and body-interface rejection. Do not equate industrial particles, combat buildup and chronic burden numerically without calibration. Exact inoculation tiers, conversion, processing rates and ordinary-versus-Hexen multiplier remain open; retain approved Hexen industrial throughput, conversion, secondary mutation and possession rules.

Untreated Hex-induced coma has 10% natural recovery, 50% Hexen transformation, 40% fatal poisoning. Ordinary effective treatment Quality I transfers 10 percentage points from fatality to recovery; Quality IV guarantees survival, not nonmutation. Intermediate linear Quality II/III values (20/30 points) follow the proposed interpolation; confirm detailed treatment procedure, stacking and Quality V additional benefits before assigning them. Living Alchemy can prevent/reverse an incomplete mutation if actual bodily Hex is extracted before the process completes; reversal of an established Hexen mutation is extraordinary, comparable to permanently reversing biological age. Conventional healing improves survival but does not itself undo mutation. Imperial emergency cybernetic replacement can address organ damage, typically lungs first, then oxygen-dependent tissues; once neurological damage reaches the brain its usefulness is severely limited. Body-interfacing implants can themselves generate chronic Hex; no blanket immunity or automatic mutation cure.

## November 25, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: modular Orbcraft progression and gadget servicing

Owner: [40_Kobold_Technology_and_Orbcraft.md](40_Kobold_Technology_and_Orbcraft.md). Orbcraft is INT-governed, not DEX-governed. Technological research primarily unlocks distinct capabilities horizontally; five root technologies grant foundational use, with advanced research extending capabilities and unlocking specialized or exotic uses. Most gadgets require only a handful of technologies; final root names, research catalogue, SP costs and prerequisites remain open. The earlier six subject divisions remain descriptive, not a fixed purchase tree.

Gadgets are permanent, economically valuable physical inventions, not temporary conjurations or a limited daily inventory. Actual materials, tools and labor are required; no generic off-screen salvage or spontaneous components. Inferior materials, excessive fuel consumption and neglected filtration make improvised devices less desirable without automatic expiration. Standardized interchangeable modules have individual Quality and functional performance. Orb implements combine general ability with specialization choices such as bandwidth, mana storage and fabrication; bandwidth comes from both equipment and expertise, exact capacities open. Integrated machines combine multiple gadgets, with energy and bandwidth determined by their actual subsystems; even remote robots require perception, propulsion, power, control and useful tools. Preserve action economy and meaningful command requirements.

Fabrication ranks I–V permit manufacturing modules of Quality I–V respectively and integrating at most 1/2/4/8/16 gadgets respectively in a single assembly. This is not a limit on owned gadgets. Higher-Quality purchased or salvaged modules may be installed with suitable technology, tools and compatibility. The former two-tier conventional weapon fabrication penalty is superseded by full qualified Fabrication Quality; no enchantment or refining permission. Ordinary improvised tools remain distinct. Module sizes are miniature, handheld, personal, vehicle and industrial. Compatible same-size transfers preserve both items and cost time alone. Increasing a module one size category consumes additional resources and fabrication time but is cheaper than manufacturing the larger module anew; destructive downsizing/reworking is possible with significant time and fabrication. Exact recipes, salvage yields, size limits and times open.

Gadget use generates Hex waste. Adequately contained ordinary use (e.g. a filtered laser pistol) does not inherently add personal Hex each shot; poorly filtered emergency gadgets (e.g. jetpack leaps) may expose the operator. Codex refueling and Hex-Cell servicing are linked: slow out-of-combat recharging permits gradual release or appropriate collection without personal exposure under suitable conditions; rapid combat refueling causes a burst of Hex under existing status rules. Environmental release remains pollution, not annihilation. Preserve stored waste leakage and existing Hexed status and augmentation Hex Rejection rules. Exact waste per MP, cell capacity, overflow handling, recharge time/action, personal buildup conversion and tracking implementation remain unresolved.

## November 24, 2026 — AUTHOR CLARIFICATION: ambient Haze persistence and ecological recovery

Ambient dispersed Haze dissipates naturally at the same rate as ordinary environmental depleted mana under comparable ecological conditions. Hex nevertheless imposes the established 8× environmental burden relative to native depleted mana while present; this is not an 8× slower inherent decay rate, a combat multiplier, or a new MP-to-Hex conversion. The barren, degraded Scarlands process environmental pollution slowly because natural ecological processing capacity is diminished, reinforcing persistent contamination. Preserve distinctions between containment leakage, fresh Hex dispersal and ambient environmental assimilation. No universal environmental half-life or numerical recovery rate is established; the existing 30-day stored-mana leakage benchmark is not automatically an ambient decay rate. The earlier assistant suggestion of an intrinsically decades-long ambient Haze half-life is not adopted. Exact assimilation thresholds, biological conversion accounting, Hexway engineering, purification upkeep, possession mechanics and demon motives remain under development. The author's playful suggestion of demon environmentalism is deferred, not confirmed canon.

Owners: 20 and 39; index updated.

## November 24, 2026 — AUTHOR ESTABLISHED: Dreamcatchers, Leshy cleanup and industrial Leydrains

Most Canopy clockwork incorporates Nullporcelain waste-management components called Dreamcatchers; average collection is about 50% of arriving depleted mana, with finite accumulation and emptying during maintenance. Nested machine, factory-floor and prosperous-city Dreamcatchers catch successive shares of remaining waste, not additive percentage points: three 50% stages capture 87.5% of original waste when functioning. Preserve Nullporcelain nonconductivity; engineered collector is not a claim that the ceramic itself absorbs energy. Captured waste may be recycled or transferred into matter for slow dispersion across regions (e.g. waterways or smokestacks); dispersion does not imply destruction, guaranteed safe disposal or zero ecological burden.

Leshy can reach deep with roots, selectively draw remaining depleted mana by color and transform it into Nectar. Preserve Nectar's nonconvertibility back into usable MP and unresolved doses, yield, skill requirements and costs. Centaur industrial Leydrains accelerate natural directional conversion red→blue→green→black→white→red, drawing depleted mana and producing pure mana of the successor color. Author wants significant inefficiency/catches; exact input, output, operating energy, residues, costs and throughput remain OPEN. Industrial Leydrain is distinct from existing Celestite Leydrain combat suppression; no alteration to divine material, spells, ranks or item costs. No assumption of Hex removal by these mechanisms. Existing concentrated depleted-mana burden multipliers remain in force.

## November 24, 2026 — AUTHOR CLARIFICATION: Beanstock geography and catastrophic death

Beanstock cultivation is nearly impossible in the Scarlands' mountains and swamps due to Hex and insufficient suitable water; color affinity does not confer Hex immunity or replace physical necessities. This is a strong regional tendency, not an absolute prohibition on extraordinary suitable sites. The more ecologically diverse Imperium can plausibly cultivate Beanstocks, opening opportunities for mutual benefit and cooperation with Canopy expertise; no specific existing Imperial plantation, treaty or ownership arrangement established. Preserve Worldspindle limits and separate Hex management.

At the literal worst-case death of a Beanstock, released pure mana may produce severe and increasingly frequent natural disasters according to its color: black — plagues; blue — extreme rainfall and flooding; red — grave earthquakes; green — explosive overgrowth of other plants; white — rapid desertification. These are catastrophic possibilities, not automatic results of ordinary wilting, routine discharge or every plant death. Magnitude, affected extent, duration, recovery and mitigation remain unresolved. Preserve distinct depleted-mana pollution burden scale and the prohibition on Beanstock Hex removal. The author considers deliberate misuse by a legendary Leshy a possible high-stakes narrative premise; feasibility, constraints and safeguards are not finalized. No new offensive Craft ability or operational procedure established.

## November 24, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: Beanstock lifecycle, color specialization and regional industry

Beanstocks are rare, geographically concentrated industrial assets, not ordinary town infrastructure. It is desirable that an efficient mature plant can outproduce its host settlement's demand and supply surrounding territory; prioritize industrial centers and regional demand when testing the approved 300,000 MP/day reference. Author accepts the preceding 100,000-person regional industrial census as a provisional target for later sector calibration, not a universal installation count or validated engineering demand: 100 farm-equivalents 4,837,500 MP/year, 400 workshops 24,000,000, 30 factories 18,000,000, 100 freight vessels 9,000,000, municipal infrastructure 10,950,000, construction/miscellaneous 7,300,000; total 74,087,500/year (~202,979/day). Refining ore should generally be substantially more energy-intensive than cutting grain; exact comparison needs engineering calibration. Do not double count a city's surrounding farms or equate theoretical supply with saleable color-compatible fuel.

Beanstocks categorically do NOT remove Hex. Preserve separate Hex management and existing environmental burden rules. Each Beanstock specializes in one of the five mana colors, ordinarily matching its native environment for practical reasons. Wild Beanstocks occur naturally in all five colors: small, well-hidden plants in mana-rich environments are among the greatest foraging discoveries, comparable to other maximum-rarity alchemical plants; some wild plants are already large enough for industrial use and virtually always house terrifying Starspawn. No fixed rarity odds, locations or harvest rules. An entire Canopy realm might have only one efficient blue Beanstock; an aggressively ley-line-utilizing black Beanstock might transform nearby ecology toward a desert or savanna relative to its surroundings. These are geographic illustrations, not a finalized inventory, mandatory black-mana biome or specific mapped location. A wilting Beanstock is a potential natural disaster, not merely lost fuel output.

A Beanstock seed requires years of investment from an existing Beanstock. Raising the plant itself takes approximately one month of sensitive cultivation, with controlled surroundings, gradually increasing mana supply and proper harvesting. Errors, interruptions or prolonged loss of the lead Leshy may stunt the final plant, make it dangerously unstable, require months of correction or cause death. A substantial team of exceptionally skilled Leshy can collectively manage a Beanstock; a legendary Leshy can manage its magical cultivation alone, and is preferred especially for resolving emergencies. Ordinary Leshy contribute little magical capability to the end result. This supersedes any strictly mandatory single legendary-cultivator requirement; mundane supporting labor, infrastructure and logistics are still separately required. Exact team size, seed cycle/yield, cultivation costs, stabilization, disaster mechanisms and recovery rates remain open.

Preserve the approved reference absorption, refining efficiency and stress bands as provisional working calibration; real demand, mana sources, colors, transport and ecological waste handling may require future adjustment. No new Craft ranks, SP/MP costs, geographic proportions, or final market prices established.

## November 24, 2026 — AUTHOR CLARIFICATION: Freeze potency and expanded Wakecraft test scope

Replacement HP/d20 prototype: Freeze is an advanced-incapacitating status and uses half ordinary outgoing status-applying Power before the applicable buildup multiplier. A pure Freeze attack under the universal 3× pure-status rule therefore has a 1.5× baseline; do not silently stack the historical dedicated Freeze 2× modifier with the new framework (reconciliation remains open). Pyromancers retain ordinary red, blue and white fire. Earlier approved flame distinctions: red delivers 100% ordinary Burning buildup and bypasses 0% armor-derived ER; blue delivers 50% buildup and bypasses 25% armor-derived ER; white delivers no buildup or refresh and bypasses 50% armor-derived ER. Wakecraft has physical Water attacks with Erosion buildup, physical piercing Ice Spikes with **no Freeze buildup** (supersedes old Ice Stab hybrid), and full pure Freeze status attacks. Water/Erosion now joins the near-term **Wakecraft** test scope, not martial elemental weapon testing. Preserve optional Erosion transfer on qualifying Freeze/Lightning contact, actual medium and casting costs, and earlier approved Freeze penalties. Fire, Lightning and Freeze remain the martial elemental test scope; defer Air, Hex, spellblades and implement tuning. No new damage or AP values for Ice Spikes, no new spell purchase costs, and no simulated results approved by this clarification.

## November 24, 2026 — AUTHOR CORRECTION: elemental status identities and narrowed research scope

HP/d20 replacement prototype: Water/Erosion reduces ER (formerly MR) by 25% at 1× and 50% at 2×; qualifying Lightning or Freeze status hits may consume Erosion, transfer all its buildup into the new status and benefit from its resistance reduction for status damage. Air increases other existing statuses as Air buildup rises; at 1× or 2× may instead consume all statuses for a damaging explosion. Lightning at 1× removes one action; at 2× stuns for the first turn and paralyzes thereafter; on triggering, buildup resets to zero while the condition remains for three turns. Hex drains MP then deals substantial HP damage once mana is dry. See `35_Magical_Media_and_Contests.md` for full correction and unresolved implementation details. Next tests restricted to Fire, Lightning and Freeze; defer Water/Air/Hex interactions, INT-scaling melee spellblades and implement tuning tradeoffs until later. No simulated results or operative-engine changes claimed.

## November 24, 2026 — AUTHOR ESTABLISHED: regional energy distribution and biological Vital Essence

Vital Essence is harvested directly from living creatures; raw mana cannot be converted into Vital Essence. Preserve all five colors, existing extraction restrictions and frozen 1–3 year spoilage benchmark. Author's economic design target: extraction should be competitive with the cost/opportunity cost of ordinary labor (including enslaved mining labor), potentially as viable as or more viable than ordinary fuel; no automatic premium, exact yield, extraction harm, recovery rate, price or labor regime established. Refrigeration is possible through enchantment, Wakecraft and alchemy; clockwork itself lacks a refrigeration solution. Do not infer new purchasable spells, ranks or MP costs.

Beanstock juice has low usable MP per unit volume/mass despite very high total plantation output; intentionally harder to ship than competing fuel media. No fixed density or plantation yield yet.

Imperium predominantly distributes energy in compact Codexes, requiring special reinforcement to avoid catastrophic detonation. Preserve modern rechargeability, ancient nonrechargeable finite reserves, color/handling restrictions and unresolved exact capacity, failure, reinforcement and retention mechanics.

Scarlands alchemical circles relay very large quantities of raw mana rapidly across linked networks, potentially much faster than parrotfolk flight. This is transmission rather than storage: without Codexes or extremely costly bulk Leywells, arriving mana needs prompt use. Most deliveries are sustained over hours or effectively continuous, not a single instantaneous discharge. Preserve existing catalyst cycle, refining stoichiometry, Hex and lawful alchemical constraints; do not equate transmission with free generation or assume every relay refines mana. Exact throughput, latency, relay spacing, losses, construction/operating costs, storage and failure mechanics remain open.

## November 24, 2026 — Author clarification: precision machinery and component value

High workmanship Quality is not synonymous with best all-round economics. High-precision performance-oriented machines may sacrifice reliability, fuel economy and service life for precision, power and output; expect substantially higher annual maintenance, potentially higher fuel use and modest or shorter service life versus ordinary commercial machinery. This supersedes the earlier illustrative premium-machine assumption of universally lower maintenance and longer life; efficient bespoke designs remain possible where designed for efficiency. Exact modifiers remain open. Distinguish raw alloy stock from fabricated precision components and assembled machines. Author prefers valuable Springsteel/Nullporcelain internals and engine/Leywell assemblies to dominate harvester value rather than structural frame. Springsteel stock meeting/exceeding frame stock value and Nullporcelain stock around 32 silver are tentative calibration preferences, subject to clarification after component-cost allocation, not approved price changes.

## November 24, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: Deflection armor and Honed weapon identity (HP/d20 replacement)

Deflection is a situational armor sidegrade, not a universal upgrade. Retain 50% of equipment-derived physical Armor Rating and add flat Evasion +1/+2/+3 for Light/Medium/Heavy respectively. Purchased armor training retains full effectiveness: effective AR = 0.5 × equipment AR + trained AR (preserve existing rounding pipeline). Ordinary weight and handling requirements remain unchanged. Training may be planned around equipment bonuses; equipping or switching armor does not automatically refund historical TP purchases. This supersedes earlier experimental total-armor reductions. Do not infer changes to shield deflection, magical resistance or the operative wound engine.

The former experimental Precision weapon identity is now named **Honed**: meticulous weight balance improves accuracy at the cost of striking power. Honed does not inherently mean lighter or lower handling requirements. Exact numerical weapon tradeoffs remain unresolved; retain historical engine identifiers for replay. Both Honed and Deflection should be situationally better or worse, preserving counterplay.

Evidence: Combat Lab jobs `fa4b18c2-92db-4a62-8b50-048e49dce108`, `...110`, `...111`, `...126`, `...127` (18,000, 12,000, 42,000, 21,000 and 21,000 encounters respectively; abbreviated IDs share the first job's prefix). Explicit reinvestment studies at L25/L100 found maximum observed pair win rates 89.5%/86.5%, no draws/timeouts; equally weighted cross-archetype comparisons show situational advantages, not universal superiority. Automatic substitution returned zero refunds in the specialized study; explicit alternative purchases verified real savings, not an in-play refund mechanic. Light Deflection tested on generalists only; spatial tactics, carrying opportunity costs, optimized reinvestment, final equipment catalogue/prices and specialty weapons remain open. Preserve approved STR/END curves and frozen historical engines.

## November 24, 2026 — Author direction: industrial machinery quality and trade

Manufacturing scale and workmanship quality are independent. Cheap factories can produce junk machinery with comparable nominal work but shorter service life, higher maintenance and somewhat lower fuel efficiency. Quality matters broadly; exact industrial Quality grades/modifiers remain open. Reference machine recipes remain fixed working examples; players may propose bespoke substitutions or omissions rather than requiring a universal modular machine system now. Omitting Nullporcelain can increase environmental damage; substituting Trufula for Boughsteel is situational and retains Trufula fire vulnerability and engineering constraints. Basic mass-produced harvesters suit bulk Cindercorn; expensive specialists and marginal fuel gains need not justify premium machines. Handmade machines can be more energy/material efficient and enable delicate high-mana alchemical gardens or allow moderately skilled Leshy to maintain/harvest specialized plants. Preserve actual Craft requirements; no free skill transfer or universal capability. Review specialized material costs and secure heavy freight/restricted trade costs upward where justified; no fixed price, tariff or lifespan approved. Factory productivity study accepted in broad direction, numerical quality/trade refinements pending.

Wakecraft haulage should be situational, alchemical transport a middle ground, and clockwork superior at scale with high investment but disadvantaged in small operations. Continuously powered alchemical anchor sigils can sustain temporary Earthworks beyond the ordinary 30-day Stonecraft-maintenance limit. ## November 24, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVED: Scarlands cave settlements, temporary Earthcraft and mine transport

Scarlands subterranean settlements prefer natural caverns, built out with living Pazara and modest but significant Earthcraft expansions. Excessive subterranean digging increases unwanted demon encounters; some cities have ignored these constraints and suffer consequences. No fixed encounter probabilities or city names established.

Temporary non-Slagstone Earthworks retain 100× conventional task productivity. They tend to crumble after 24 hours without Stonecraft maintenance; with continuous upkeep they may last up to 30 days, requiring nearly as much mana and labor as initial construction (exact maintenance cadence and totals unresolved). Continuously mana-fed alchemical anchor sigils can also stabilize them; whether anchors extend beyond 30 days remains unresolved. Permanent conventional stoneworking retains 5×; Slagstone remains the stable Earthcraft exception. Dirtmoles excel at extraction; Nymbrin excel at purification. Do not infer a numerical ore-separation multiplier.

Scarlander alternatives to Centaur clockwork include Wakecraft batch haulage: miners extract ore into available tunnel capacity, withdraw for lunch or overnight, then Wakecrafters flood prepared mine routes and guide ore upward with controlled existing water. Better-equipped operations may load ore into Skyvein-lined buoyant carts, sufficiently buoyant in water with rocky payloads but not necessarily airborne. Preserve Skyvein inertia and Vital Essence upkeep. Alchemical anchor-powered elevators/lifts and conveyors are valid industrial concepts. Exact hydraulics, capacities, mana, infrastructure, safety, drainage and staffing remain open. Clockwork is the preferred superior long-term technology given extensive investment; no universal cost or throughput advantage fixed.

Efficient personal anchor upkeep follows ordinary spell upkeep with one extra Duration step free (latest author clarification); preserve the existing lawful refresh procedure, actual blue mana, accessible intact anchor and connection requirements, and other Wetcraft constraints. Do not interpret the extra Duration step as free refresh, a numerical MP discount, or an automatic benefit to externally pumped industrial mana. Industrial mana-fed anchor efficiency/cost remains adjustable. Preserve lawful Wakecraft existing-water and alchemical Hex/material constraints.

## November 24, 2026 — Earthcraft excavation, prospecting and structural stability (AUTHOR APPROVED)

Dirtmole Earthgliding moves the practitioner through earth by manipulating material around their body for propulsion. Earth Carving uses raw Rock-Craft to shave/remove chunks of earth or rock; distinguish travel from excavation. Author accepts revised excavation working benchmarks 100× ordinary, 1,000× exceptional top 2%, 10,000× legendary nested top 2%, relative to conventional excavation only (weighted 121.6× at equal utilization). Mineral detection is a core Earthcraft function with at least 20× conventional prospecting capability; separate detection from ore separation, whose 5× candidate remains unapproved. Ore and especially rare ore are harder to find in accessible locations: iron may be as geologically common as terrestrial iron, but deposits not associated with demon nests are much scarcer. Distinguish geological abundance, discovery, access/security and ore grade; no fixed nest frequency.

Raw Earth Carving is inherently unstable for construction. Alchemical anchor sigils can stabilize such structures at continuous mana cost, preserving existing lawful alchemy and Hex constraints. Temporary structures (e.g. stone scaffolding) assist proper construction. Permanent conventional stoneworking/construction tasks assisted by Earthcraft use a Leshy-like 5× ordinary productivity reference, superseding proposed 20× stone shaping and 10× stabilization as general long-term construction assumptions. Earthcraft assists masonry rather than replacing it. Slagstone is an explicit exception: Earthcraft enables its easy molding and stable structures. Exact mana requirements, structural duration, failure behavior, recipes, prospecting success, mine support and playable mechanics remain open. Scarlanders may have alternatives to Centaur clockwork; specifics unresolved.

## November 23, 2026 — D20 ACCURACY/EVASION ANALYTICAL AUDIT AFTER CONFIRMATION CLARIFICATION

**ANALYTIC FINDINGS ONLY, NOT A COMBAT LAB SIMULATION OR NEW CANON:** For an ordinary attack where natural 20 already meets the ordinary attack target, write `H = P(d20 + actual Attack >= actual defense)`. The natural-20 confirmed-critical rule with the **same snapshotted** attack/defense on the second independent d20 gives `P(confirmed critical per attack) = (1/20) × H` and therefore `P(critical | landed hit) = 1/20 = 5%`. If a confirmed attack critical inflicts ×2 postmitigation damage, mean dealt damage per attempt is `1.05 × H × ordinary landed HP damage` (ignoring other attack effects). In the ordinary unsaturated d20 range, **+1 Attack** increases `H` by 5 percentage points and confirmed-critical chance by 0.25 percentage points; **+1 defender Evasion** reduces them by the same amounts. This does **not** independently approve any natural-20 auto-hit rule for an attack total that cannot reach the target.

**Illustrative equal-investment neutral reference fighters (not final builds):** At L10, STR specialist 28/18/28, hybrid 23/23/28, DEX specialist 18/28/28 (STR/DEX/END) give base derived Attack/Evasion **1/1, 1/1, 1/2**. At L50, 76/26/76, 51/51/76, 26/76/76 give **4/4, 3/5, 3/5**. At L100, 136/36/136, 86/86/136, 36/136/136 give **7/7, 6/8, 5/10**, with no purchased proficiency ranks or modifiers. A hybrid attacking a same-attribute-investment STR specialist has hit chance **55% at L10, 50% at L50 and 50% at L100**; +1 temporary Attack makes these **60%/55%/55%**, while using +1 temporary Evasion instead reduces the STR specialist's reciprocal hit chances from **55%/50%/50%** to **50%/45%/45%**. New confirmed-critical probability when hit chance is 50% is **2.5% per attempted attack**, versus **2.75%** for 55% chance to hit. These examples omit weapon choice, equal SP spending, armor, tactics, racial differences and dynamic Coordination; they do not establish actual duel win rates.

**Balance implication:** The old coupling of attack accuracy with margin-10 critical frequency is removed in this normal case. +1 still matters substantially, especially for constrained hit rates, but is no longer a combined automatic five-percentage-point increase in both accuracy and critical probability. Coordination +1/+2/+3/+4 must be re-evaluated under a newly versioned worker with actual per-turn selection; prior Coordination duel win rates use superseded margin criticals. The exact natural-20 auto-hit edge case remains open. No live worker deployment or newly simulated duels claimed.

## November 23, 2026 — AUTHOR CLARIFICATION: EXACT SAME ATTACK AND DEFENSE ON CRITICAL CONFIRMATION

**APPROVED HP/d20 replacement-prototype procedure:** After the initial natural **20** threatens an attack critical, make an **independent confirmation d20 against the SAME actual defense target as the initial attack** and apply the **SAME actual hit bonus as on that initial attack**, **including temporary/situational bonuses and penalties** on either side. Snapshot the relevant attack modifier and defending AC at primary attack resolution; neither side loses benefits or penalties merely because confirmation is rolled afterward. Use the existing inclusive `confirmation_d20 + original_hit_bonus >= original_defense_target` test. A success preserves the approved **×2 post-mitigation HP damage** (and qualifying status buildup); a failure means **normal landed damage**. The confirmation is not an extra offensive action or second hit.

**Supersession:** This resolves the preceding “base AC” ambiguity and removes its diagnostic-only caveat about counting temporary bonuses; the older interpretation “confirmation against unmodified/base defense” is **not operative** in this prototype. Existing margin-based attack criticals are already superseded by the natural-20-plus-confirmation rule. Unresolved independently: whether natural-20 initial attack auto-hits an otherwise impossible target, if at all. Preserve general skill critical categories and operative wound engine.

**Testing:** An actual updated Combat Lab experiment is still needed. With a valid natural-20 threat, `p_critical = 0.05 × p_confirmation`, and `p_confirmation` uses the exact original modified Attack-versus-defense values. Prior 228,000 Coordination duels and the still-connected Lab 0.8.0 are **old margin-crit evidence**, not tests under this replacement rule.

**Files:** `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md` (full rule), `10_Canon_Changelog.md` (approval/supersession), `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md` (controlling current rule). No weapon, SP, MP, Quality, material or pricing change.

## November 23, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: NATURAL-20 CRITICAL THREAT + SECOND ROLL TO CONFIRM (HP/D20)

**Author-approved experimental replacement rule:** The first attack d20 must show a **natural 20** for an attack to threaten a critical hit. The attacker makes **a second confirmation roll against the target's base AC**; successful confirmation gives the existing critical damage result (**×2 post-armor damage**, and applicable doubled hostile status buildup), while a failed confirmation means **normal landed damage**, not a critical. This supersedes the HP/d20 prototype's old **margin >= +10 critical-attack success** trigger, but does **not** automatically replace unrelated nonattack skill-check critical categories or rewrite the operative quadratic/wound combat engine. Ordinary Accuracy/Evasion, their price, equipment/Weapon Ratings, action costs and other approved mechanics persist unless separately superseded.

**Unresolved technical definition:** No distinct formula for the term **base AC** is currently explicit in the HP/d20 reference: ordinary direct attacks target `10 + Evasion`. For **analytic diagnostics only**, use an independent second d20 with relevant Attack against `10+Evasion` and the already approved >= ordinary-hit convention. Whether "base" excludes situational conditions, whether natural 20 is an automatic hit if standard attack total would miss, whether critical-failure handling changes and special attack-roll exceptions are **not newly approved**. Do not silently settle these in a deployed simulator.

**Exact per-attempt math under diagnostic base-AC interpretation, not a Lab simulation:** With `delta=Attack−Evasion`, p_hit is the share of ordinary initial d20 rolls where `d20+delta>=10`; old p_crit is the share where `d20+delta>=20`; new p_crit is `0.05×p_confirm` for otherwise valid 20 hits. At delta −4/−2/0/+2/+4/+8, respective old critical chances **0%/0%/5%/15%/25%/45%** change to **1.75%/2.25%/2.75%/3.25%/3.75%/4.75%**. In a specific earlier delta −1→0 boundary case, expected normal-hit-damage multiples shift under old rules from 0.50 to 0.60 (+20%), versus new proposed confirmation probabilities from 0.525 to 0.5775 (+10%). These are **exact arithmetic for the expressly labeled test assumption**, not approved final AC wording, win rates or successful execution of an updated worker.

**Documentation:** Owning rule in `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md`; newest precedence and test status in `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md`. Next: versioned Combat Lab support and real simulations against varied builds before final Coordination selection.

**Approved experimental correction, not a live operative change:** In the replacement HP/d20 system, qualifying Both-stat weapon damage uses **`A_Both = effective STR + effective DEX`**, replacing the November 22 Batch 1 factor `0.65 × (STR + DEX)` for subsequent experimental calculations. ## November 22, 2026 — AUTHOR CORRECTION: 25% PASSABLE/50% LARGE WALL BREACH, LOCAL SECTION TARGET AND MAGNITUDE

**Supersedes previous 10%/25% wall-hole thresholds** of the HP/d20 prototype. A **passable hole** for a creature/person is produced by **at least 25% of the local targeted wall section's maximum HP** in actual post-armor damage; a **large hole**, allowing multiple people to squeeze through, requires **50%**. Without sufficient legal Magnitude, attacks are assumed to hit only **one fairly small section** of a wall and leave the rest mainly intact. To damage a larger wall area or an **entire castle at once**, the effect needs lawful sufficiently large **Magnitude/area coverage** rather than just concentrated Power. If a local section is **completely destroyed**, the rest of the connected wall **might suffer about 10% HP loss** from structural instability where appropriate, not a blanket automatically inflicted castle-wide 10%. Exact wall subsection area, individual section HP, whether damage sums over multiple hits for hole classification, and how Magnitude extends structural coverage remain unresolved.

**Approval scope:** Replacement-prototype mechanical direction; preserve operative structure/wound engine and other approved material/enchanted/equipment behavior until converted. Owning documents updated: `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md`, `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md`, `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md` and this changelog. No simulation was run.

**Approved new HP/d20 replacement-prototype equipment/object durability direction:** **Light shield = half the maximum ordinary HP of a level-matched generalist fighter, protected by light-equivalent armor**; **Medium shield = half that generalist HP, armor equal to the generalist's armor**; **Heavy shield = twice the half-HP amount (equal to the generalist HP), armor equivalent to heavy armor**. Do not invent new absolute numbers, quarter-HP for Light or double-HP for Heavy; reference generalist loadout and rounding remain open.

Wall armor follows the corresponding level's **medium-armored END specialist spending all eligible Weight on armor**. The five reference classes are **thin wood L1, normal wood L10, thin stone L25, thick stone L75, steel L100**. This fixes relative armor targets, but NOT absolute wall HP, wall-panel geometry, damage accumulation per localized region, shield Guard overflow/breakage, real material/Quality equivalent values, enchantment numbers or equipment prices.

## November 22, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: BURNING ROUND UP/FIRST TICK; FIRE, ASH, WATER, ICE, HEX AND THREADS

**Burning:** Per tick `ceil(max ordinary HP / 3)`; no Shimmer Guard addition to the damage basis. **The first tick occurs at the end of the affected victim's next proper turn**, including Severity I; thereafter Severity I ticks every other victim turn, Severity II every victim turn, always end-of-turn. This supersedes the prior assistant suggestion to delay the Severity I first tick to the end of the second affected turn. Legal extinguishing before the tick prevents scheduled damage if Burning is cleared. Rounding is now decided; Shimmer absorption, on-victim-turn application and severity-change cadence remain open.

**Media exclusivity and reaction:** Fire and hot ash **exclude one another**; fire and water, puddles or ice **exclude one another**. When fire meets water/puddles, the **fire becomes cold ash** and **water becomes steam**; when fire meets ice, **fire becomes cold ash** and **ice becomes water**. Fire **may coexist with Hex and magical threads**, respecting their ordinary physical/source eligibility. **Cold ash is not hot ash**, and is not automatically a 0.5× Burning buildup hazard. No unsanctioned steam damage/obscuration, area growth or automatic creature-Burning removal is added. Preserve the previously approved terrain 1× fire Burning, 1× Hex Hexed, 0.5× hot ash Burning rates and per-status once-per-turn limit. Fine-scale medium amounts, contact timing and multi-source overlaps remain open.

**Scope and files:** Approved for the HP/d20 replacement prototype only; old operative combat reference and old elements mechanics remain until migration. Updated `35_Magical_Media_and_Contests.md`, `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md`, `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md`, and `10_Canon_Changelog.md`. No Combat Lab simulation run.

In the HP/d20 replacement prototype, **Burning at standard Severity I** deals **33% of the victim's maximum ordinary HP at the END of EVERY OTHER victim turn**; **advanced Severity II** deals **33% of maximum ordinary HP at the END of EVERY victim turn**. For the **HP/d20 replacement prototype**, the attacking Jester **chooses the part affected by a qualifying standard Binding**. ## November 22, 2026 — AUTHOR-APPROVED D20, PRESSURE AND HP-STATUS REPLACEMENT PROTOTYPE; STATUS COUNTERS

**Author decisions approved for future integrated replacement, NOT CURRENT OPERATIVE WOUND/QUADRATIC ENGINE:** Purchased proficiency ranks start at zero, are earned, and purchased universal Attack serves both martial and magical accuracy; STR+half DEX martial, INT+half DEX magical, END+half DEX Evasion. Movement is renamed Athletics and used for swimming/climbing/acrobatics; Initiative becomes Reflex, used to roll initiative and relevant AoE escapes. General checks `d20+proficiency >= DC` (DC 5–35), crit at +10 margin, critical failure at −10 margin, no natural 1/20 automatic critical. Direct attack `d20+Attack >= 10+Evasion`; AoE escape `d20+Reflex >= 10+spell Attack`. Successful critical attacks double damage **and status buildup**, with temporary accuracy/evasion adjusting actual critical odds. AoE partial damage remains effect-specific. Two-action and one-offensive-attack limits retained.

**Pressure author override:** Net Pressure 1/2/3 applies −2/−4/−6 to both Evasion and Reflex; **3 PP automatically Trapped**, contrary to the older separate-position-only Trapped interpretation *in this prototype*. Defensive actions do not fire when Trapped but eligible passive automatic shield interception remains. Old separate Extreme Pressure/Guard interactions need explicit conversion.

**Status math author direction:** Current ordinary HP replaces separate SR; Hero minimum effective status HP = 25% maximum ordinary HP. Standard severity at 1× effective status HP; advanced/incapacitating at 2×. Damaging status spells deal 1× damage + 1× buildup; pure status spells produce 3× buildup, and an advanced-incapacitating magical attack halves effective outgoing Power for application before the buildup coefficient. Critical successes double buildup; these are actual attacks requiring legal accuracy. Default test assumes ordinary MR affects damage but not status buildup unless a named counter/interception applies, subject to future material tests. Status builds refresh with each new eligible application (three-round window). Lowering HP alone does not change status intensity; a qualifying new status application triggers severity recalculation. Status reduction also downgrades already active severity immediately when thresholds crossed.

**Counters/durations:** Generally an allied counter reduces 0.5× effective status HP of standard buildup or 0.25× of advanced buildup per eligible action; special complete extinguishes (e.g. water on actual Burning) remove all buildup. Freeze ice can be damaged, Binding threads severed, living-Polymorph sigil scars healed, and qualifying psychic effects addressed through Encourage. Conscious isolated Sleep and Charm victims have no ordinary physical self-reduction. **Sleep I = −2 AC and −2 all d20 checks, conscious**; advanced Sleep incapacitates for **one minute**, removable by shaking/damaging sleeper. Many other advanced immobilizations require active removal, though ice can naturally melt over many minutes. An existing old “Sleep 3” phrase is noted without inventing a third severity rank. Shimmer Guard does not ordinarily resist statuses; while dormant, a Hero may break it to reduce an otherwise defeating status to 1×, timing details open.

**Numerical calibration only, not simulated:** Baseline 300 HP, spell Power100: unprotected direct damage in three successful hits; pure incapacitating status `100×0.5×3=150` buildup/hit against 600 advanced threshold, four successful hits; 40%/50% illustrative MR damage mitigation yields five/six damage hits. This is an intended successful-hit benchmark, NOT promised real-turn victory count or historical matchup replication. Reconcile generic Nymbrin 2× specialty Transmogrified, former Jestercraft full effective Binding Power, Encourage INT², existing Fire/Ice/Water attacks and old typed SR, armor/MR/shield details, duration, math rounding and Hit-vs-HP ordering. No Combat Lab experiment was executed.

**Documentation:** Updated owning Combat and Magic status sections, Psycraft/Jestercraft/Nymbrin prototype migration notices, index and changelog. Historical operative passages remain for provenance rather than being silently deleted.

## November 22, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: 100% Shimmer Reserve and 51%-of-COMBINED-HP emergency Break for additive-HP prototype

**Explicitly approved design:** Hero Shimmer Guard provides a reserve equal to **100% of maximum ordinary HP** in the experimental additive-HP replacement. While intact and dormant, a single attack's **post-armor HP damage >=51% of maximum combined ordinary+Shimmer HP** is **completely negated**, Shimmer Guard **breaks**, the entire unused reserve is lost, and there is **no Shimmer benefit for 24 hours**. Emergency applies while dormant, not after the reserve is already active.

## November 22, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: all wound-based attribute and combat penalties removed

**Decision:** The author explicitly approves complete removal of wound-based penalties. Wounded, Gravely Wounded, and Hero/Legend Shimmer Guard injury stages do not reduce STR, DEX, END, INT, SPD, Combat Speed, attack Power, Defense Power, hit/evasion difficulty, equipment eligibility, or any other combat calculation. No percentage, flat, situational, pain-based, or simplified wound penalty replaces the removed rules. Pain may be narrated but has no mechanical penalty. **Incapacitated** remains the existing state that ordinarily prevents action.

**Preserved:** Ordinary characters retain three injury advancements. Heroes and Legends retain two additional Shimmer Guard injury stages; Guard I and Guard II are additional injury capacity, not low-penalty stages. Existing injury thresholds, number of advancements from attacks, healing, prognosis, Shimmer presentation, and Hero/Legend distinctions remain unchanged. Independent hostile statuses and their explicitly approved effects are unaffected.

**Supersedes:** The former Wounded −5%, Gravely Wounded −10%, and Incapacitated −15% effective-attribute penalties; the Hero/Legend “still −5%” Guard stages; wound-triggered equipment qualification/shortfall recalculations; and references to wounds reducing initiative Combat Speed. Historical simulations that used wound penalties remain historical and are not current balance evidence.

**Files changed:** `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md` (owning injury and equipment-shortfall rules), `01_World_and_Shimmer.md` (Shimmer Guard cross-reference), `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md` (equipment shortfall and historical stress-test notes), `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md` (current summary), and this changelog.

**Simulation compatibility:** Combat Lab 0.7.0's warrior engine still applies the old wound factor and does not implement Attack/Defense Grades. Its full-duel outputs do not yet represent this approval. No simulator code was changed in this canon update; a separate engine update is required before full duels can test the revised rules.

## November 22, 2026 — Author approval: binding as status attack, full magic Attack Power, unlimited separate captives, reusable Draped mines

**Universal combat ACTION classification approved:** **All active actions that attempt to inflict hostile status effects are ATTACKS**, regardless of direct damage. They consume the existing one-offensive-attack-action-per-turn allowance and their otherwise applicable one-/two-action procedures and costs; this is not an invented extra attack or free casting loophole. Failed status attack attempts still consume their committed attack actions. This applies to Jester Binding and other pure-status attacks; nonoffensive removal of an existing condition and unrelated ongoing passive condition triggers are not new separately committed attacks merely by being status-related. Owning `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md`.

**Jestercraft Binding Power now approved:** **`P_Binding(MP) = P_ordinary_magic_attack(MP)`** for the exact same lawful base offensive mana expenditure and other eligible spell Power modifiers, preserving the currently approved ordinary offensive attack multiplier formula. No bespoke Binding Power penalty or pure-status doubling and no direct wounds from this Binding are implied. Existing Bound status stages/counters and lawful magic, medium, source range and resistance still apply.

**Perpetually reusable source versus paid emitted restraints approved:** A Draped floor/rug/web tile or Jester's own usable Worn Draped origin serves as the **renewable physical/magical starting point for new binding threads woven FROM the invested mana**. Previously described “binding fiber comes from the source environment” is clarified/superseded insofar as it implied consuming or pulling apart the source rug: **the source material itself is not used up, downgraded, damaged, cleared, nor turned into free inventory Stitches merely by launching a legal Binding**. Each distinct Binding still costs its own legal offensive attack action and mana. The same rug can legally threaten new targets on later turns and works as a repeatedly usable mine rather than a one-use trap or automatically triggered zero-MP trap.

**Independent captives and persistence:** There is **no innate numerical limit on concurrently bound targets**; each captive separately undergoes the lawful attack, buildup and **individual escape** procedure. A captive who legally succeeds in escaping is free of that Binding. Preexisting helpless thresholds can preclude personal self-escape until resolved by another legitimate means. Escaping or cutting a personal restraint never by itself clears the Draped floor tile; a combatant must directly remove/destroy the source to clear its persistent ability to launch new restraints. Effects on already active emitted threads if a source is later destroyed remain unapproved. Other open implementation issues: Binding's precise one-versus-two-action variants and to-hit/resistance integration, per-escape action costs/difficulty, material durability and source destruction geometry; no new actual mana price or auto-area attack granted.

**Owner/cross-references:** `05_Jestercraft.md` for Binding; `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md` for universal attack classification; `35_Magical_Media_and_Contests.md` for magical Power and medium; `10_Canon_Changelog.md` for approvals; `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md` for latest navigation. Older statements that the Binding consumes material from an origin are superseded by this entry.

## November 22, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Technique uses highest STR/DEX; four Draped tiles per Stitch; one Worn Stitch qualifies

**LATEST universal combat-stat revision:** `Technique = max(effective STR, effective DEX)`. Choose whichever effective attribute is higher, accounting for existing modifiers. This **supersedes globally** the November 16 `Technique=2×effective STR+effective DEX`, earlier grapple-control `G=2×STR+DEX`, and those old formulas where repeated in grapple, Feint and Unravel descriptions. Preserve the original universal opposed-check defender/attacker ratio to six Naked-d20 categories, existing Technique-required maneuvers, controls, action costs and legal physical reach. Specialized STR and DEX warriors now can compete on comparable Technique scores; high INT alone does not increase the statistic. Historical old-formula references below must be read as **explicitly superseded**, not active rules.

**LATEST environmental fabric/drapery approval:** **One whole Stitch can produce FOUR actual qualifying Draped 5-foot terrain tiles**, under already approved lawful Unravel source access, real anchors/paths, `max(1,ceil(full Jestercraft CL/5))` source-Stitch throughput per action, and the **single highest eligible enemy controller's Technique** opposed check wherever new fabric enters real hostile zones. One source Stitch remains indivisible and cannot supply more than its own total approved `0.5×eligible defensive spell Power` in protective Defense just because it spans four tiles. The four-Draped-**tiles** ratio is now controlling, **not** the previous proposed `4 Threaded/2 Woven/1 Draped 20-foot tightropes` ratio as a restriction on Draped tile footprint; independently valid rope geometry still needs resolution. Fabric remains physically deployed and is not consumed/downgraded simply for Binding.

**AUTHOR-APPROVED mobile Draped source:** A Jester wearing **at least one usable Stitch** of their own Regalia **counts as Draped** for normal Jestercraft Binding; thus a target within ordinary **5-foot melee/Short Reach** may be bound from the Jester as the source. **Three Stitches for torso coverage remain a separate defensive-coverage requirement**; no three-Stitch requirement for being a mobile Draped binding origin. Environmental Draped tiles continue to enable binding within five feet of themselves, even when the Jester is farther away subject to lawful contact/medium. The number of creatures that can be kept bound from an intact terrain source, precise physical tile-to-rope conversion and distributed damage for one Stitch covering four Draped tiles are unresolved; no new MP/casting schedule or free extra attacks is invented.

**APPROVED:** Environmental **Unravel and Weave** each cost **one action**, manipulating up to `U(CL)=max(1,ceil(full applicable Jestercraft CL/5))` whole Stitch-equivalents from **one eligible physically accessible source tile** (including the Jester's Worn Regalia as source), without additional MP to merely reshape **already enchanted** material. CL1–5 =1 Stitch/action, 6–10=2, 11–15=3, 16–20=4, 21–25=5, 26–30=6. This does **not** cap number of affected ropes/tiles by one, permit free fabric creation or change Regalia's approved native cap `5+floor(full CL/2)`. Moving **all fabric while still Worn** remains a distinct innate **one-action** rearrangement exempt from the environmental throughput limit and one-action half-CL spellcasting cap. The Jester's existing 1-MP-per-Stitch enchantment cost for newly prepared eligible external cloth remains intact.

**AUTHOR CORRECTION versus assistant's per-defender recommendation:** An Unravel attempt to place/advance fabric into hostile real control-zone tiles calls for **one opposed Technique check against the HIGHEST eligible defending creature's Technique**, just as in the existing strongest-controller movement rule. Not one check per defender/rope/tile. Defender must actually be able to control challenged terrain under reach, geometry and availability. Success permits otherwise lawful placement; failure blocks those defended squares for that action, not unrelated legitimately unopposed placements. No automatic free damage, reaction, destruction of source cloth, or blanket Threadwalk movement bonus applies to this remote deployment check. One exceptional warrior can shield backline squares in their genuine control zone.

**JESTERCRAFT BINDING RANGE/MEDIUM APPROVED:** Binding is **Short Reach originating from Draped environmental fabric**: an eligible intended target must be within **5 feet of a qualifying Draped tile/source**. The established source fabric is *not consumed, downgraded to Woven/Threaded or erased* upon use; Binding strands arise from the existing environment and do **not cost additional whole Stitches from the worn native Regalia**. The attack still requires its lawful action, magical/physical Power/resistance/MP where applicable and previously approved Bound status; no long-range direct-from-inventory binding is authorized without a future purchased upgrade. If the Jester's own Worn Regalia **counts as Draped**, it serves as a mobile origin for melee-range Binding, as the author described; minimum worn fabric configuration to qualify as Draped remains OPEN. No unapproved Jester MP schedule, automatic restraint against all people in a Draped tile, limit on simultaneous ties, or universal change to Nymbrin/Wakecraft area environmental-binding prices follows from this decision.

**Supersession/owner:** Existing subject and index notes describing only per-source-stock Unravel pacing and one-rope-per-action are historical; the approved separate **CL/5 whole-Stitch throughput** and one strongest hostile controller now govern. The **4 Threaded/2 Woven/1 Draped 20-foot rope** numerical geometry and distributed rope durability remain illustrative pending separate explicit adoption. Owning `05_Jestercraft.md`, combat cross-reference `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md`, magical-medium cross-reference `35_Magical_Media_and_Contests.md`; summary `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md`.

## November 22, 2026 — APPROVED: Jester native Stitch capacity, innate repositioning and new Feint combat action

**Jestercraft author approval supersedes immediately earlier provisional native-capacity statements:** Native Regalia Stitch cap is **`C = 5 + floor(full applicable Jestercraft Channel Limit / 2)`**, independent of raw level and not increased by environmental harvesting, temporary enchanted external fabric, or mere recovery. Existing Cloth coverage/defense approval remains: 3 Stitches per ordinary humanoid torso covering, 8 per complete humanoid body, **0.5× eligible defensive spell Power per defending Stitch**. Under the cap formula, maximum stock supports bare-torso 2/3/4 full coverings at **CL ≥2/8/14**; full body plus those reinforced torso coverings uses 11/14/17 Stitches and requires **CL ≥12/18/24**. These are physical stock benchmarks, not a bypass of per-working CL or a new final formula for defensive spell Power. The still-in-calibration general INT+Mastery formula supplies the actual full CL for test fixtures. The historic `20 + floor(Mmax/4)` Stitch limit and separate capacity growth per Craft upgrades are superseded in the Jestercraft modernization.

**One-action defense exemption APPROVED:** Repositioning **already enchanted Worn Stitches** into the previously approved **single-location prepared protective configuration** is an **innate one-action physical Regalia action**, **not a fresh mana-costing spell** and thus **not constrained by the general one-action half-CL spell-throughput cap**. Actual separately cast magic, its legal material investment, full applicable CL, MP payments, declared triggers, physical reach, action economy and damage/Frayed attrition remain operative. The Regalia does not freely reposition after preparation or gain a second defense from this exception.

**Universal Feint combat action APPROVED:** **1 action**, credible false attack that **requires winning an opposing Technique check** using the current `Technique = max(effective STR, effective DEX)` (replacing the historical `2 × effective STR + effective DEX`). If successful against an eligible prepared defense, the Feint **forces its prepared response to trigger/commit to the apparent attack line without a real damaging strike**; on failed check no baited defensive expenditure. A successful Feint against a Jester may misposition prepared fabric or waste prepared Parry/magical defense, but **does not damage or erase a physical shield's existing barrier Defense**, automatically bypass normal shield Guard, or make permanent defenses vanish. Feint itself delivers no injury/Attack Power and does not award Parry Pressure Points. **Unresolved, not approved:** whether Feint uses the single offensive-attack allowance; assistant recommends treating it as a nondamaging setup action to allow a normal one-action Quick Attack as the second action. Specific prepared-trigger legality, attack geometry and unusual timing/counterdeception need reconciliation with the existing physical tabletop pilot and shared magical preparation rules; do not silently add extra attacks/reactions.

## November 22, 2026 — Author direction: prepared Curtainwall, enchanting external cloth, and defensive attrition

**New author-approved Jestercraft migration directions:** One action rearranges Worn Stitches into a **stationary guard at one specified body location**, able to intercept **any number of attacks aimed at that location** until barrier Defense is consumed; it does not jump between locations. Author favors a **two-action dynamically repositioning guard** but exact resolution remains OPEN. A legendary Jester should be able to stop even massive singular attacks while losing finite protection; partial damage persists, exhausted layers Fray, and partially damaged material can be spent as Frayed or kept. **One consumed Stitch repairs all partial damage on damaged fabric currently Worn**; no restoration of fully Frayed/Cut Stitches is implied, and bulk repair efficacy/timing requires balance review.

**Enchanted fabric:** Author-approved term for Jester-prepared environmental cloth that can physically slither into Regalia as stock. Can be enchanted **without wearing at 1 MP per Stitch-equivalent**. This is a specific Regalia interaction, not ordinary Leywell item enchanting, free teleportation, free matter creation or extra native capacity. Suggested limit of **~200% native Stitch capacity enchanted at a time including worn/off-body** remains **provisional**. Native capacity must grow through progression sufficiently for a properly developed level-100 Jester to have **four torso shield layers**; progression curve remains unapproved. Channel Limit still limits Stitches committed per spell and physical material contact remains required.

**Unapproved numerical stress tests** of `layers × defensive spell Power` are in `05_Jestercraft.md` (INT15/40/150 illustrative barriers 1,802/14,407.5/223,236 versus 547.56/5,776/181,135.36 physical attack Power).
