## November 22, 2026 — Jestercraft migration decisions (author-approved directions; defensive math pending)

**Status:** The following design directions were explicitly approved by the author in conversation. This is a migration addendum, not a completed rewrite of legacy Jestercraft. Preserve the old ledgers as historical references where their mechanical replacements have not been finalized.

- **Rag Doll tier-0 mobility:** Every Jester gains innate, mana-free Threadwalking: balance and travel along even a single suitably supporting taut thread, including thread-covered walls, ceilings, and suspended routes. From a Threaded or denser launch point, Threadspring permits a leap up to **half normal movement speed in any direction**, including vertically, as part of the applicable movement expenditure; it does not award unlimited free jumps. Advanced Rag Doll/D20 hit avoidance remain to be designed.
- **Environmental fabric:** Threaded → Woven → Draped is the approved escalating fabric-density concept. Another qualifying fabric application upgrades Threaded to Woven and Woven to Draped; **Woven tiles are difficult terrain for non-Jesters**. Draped fabric can serve as a required origin for powerful area binding; exact costs, power, deployment rates and other thresholds remain OPEN. Enemy clothing, furnishings, carpeting, and available fur are potential material sources, **not automatically controlled magical fabric**. Conversion requires legitimate contact/technique; helpless victims may have accessible fabric/fur unraveled. Environmental materials do not automatically increase native Regalia capacity.
- **Material contact:** Deployment does **not** require permanent connection to the Regalia, but Regalia fabric must reach the area by lawful physical means, and **the Regalia must touch fabric to transmit mana for each new magical working**. Ongoing spell contact needs are effect-specific, not presumed perpetual.
- **Stitch stock and capacity:** The intended redesigned Regalia may hold far fewer Stitches than the old ledger. Each Regalia has a finite native Stitch holding capacity; collecting material from the environment is a **cheap but not free replenishment**, not an increase to that capacity. A Regalia's applicable **Channel Limit independently restricts how many Stitches may be allocated into one spell**; conversion between CL and Stitch count is OPEN. Physical reclamation should be cheaper than generating new material magically; exact resource costs remain OPEN. A provisional simplified baseline is **seven Stitches for ordinary full humanoid-body coverage** (head/neck 1, torso 2, both arms/hands 2, both legs/feet 2); still subject to Curtainwall balance, layering, and body size.
- **Bound direction:** A physical accumulative binding condition initially restricts limbs, at **4× applicable resistance** allows escape attempts only, and at **12×** leaves the target helpless and unable to attempt self-escape. Slashing attacks directly reduce buildup at full effective eligible cutting Power; Piercing at half, and bites/claws/unarmed tearing and brute force may be viable depending on method. Escape interactions with anatomy, spell duration, status resistance, cutting material, and assistance remain to be fully reconciled. This replaces neither the global status framework nor the separate environmental restraint rules by implication.
- **Class redesign:** Hemweaving's old bespoke purchase tree and Tailor's Measure are to be retired in the migration. Black Masquerade becomes a core mode, Seamcraft a foundational ability, Curtainwall undergoes a numerical redesign, and Rag Doll retains its identity. The author proposes future Jestercraft–Drider racial linkage, more common Driders and a two-legged/six-armed subordinate spiderfolk subspecies; **these lore proposals are NOT yet canon**, and existing Drider racial lore and artifact-bound Regalia remain in effect until explicitly reconciled.
- **Curtainwall proposal, NOT YET APPROVED:** Explore a physical, expendable, actively prepared fabric shield rather than treating all ordinary flexible Regalia as traditional armor. Layered fabric could provide defensive spell Power per layer, with incoming attack Power consuming barrier capacity, fully depleted layers becoming Frayed, and later hardened Regalia granting conventional armor at possible movement cost. Precise formula, partial-layer damage tracking, bypass/overflow, action timing, armor interaction, baseline layer durability and multi-attack behavior are unresolved and must be tested against established combat rules. No numerical replacement is adopted yet.

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR ECOLOGY HYPOTHESES: Celestial Realm non-reproduction and pollinated Mossback litters

**PENDING FINAL ECOLOGY/SPECIES RATIFICATION, recorded for continuity:** Author believes Starspawn **cannot reproduce in the Celestial Realm** (a further reason to migrate to Mystaria) and that most Starspawn returning to Mystaria do so as **adults**. This would supersede the earlier implication of continuous births inside the infinite Celestial Realm, while maintaining Astral Heart immortality and ecological impossibility of ordinary permanent extinction (local disappearance remains possible). Returned Starspawn can seek preferred habitats and may reappear within species' regional range, but **a slaughtered farm animal does not seek its former ranch**, and no guaranteed exact spawn location is approved.

**Proposed Mossback biology:** **pollination-based reproduction**, very large **herd-sized broods/sprouts**, avoiding elephant gestational bottlenecks; a reproducing mother may temporarily become largely **immobile and dependent on sunlight**, function as a milk producer, then become approximately **half her former height and half her former mass** and recover over **several years**. Young Mossbacks are raised and rapidly grow on **plains fields**, later transferred/captured into fortified forest ranches near the end of their managed productive lifespan; many forest animals are captured in hunts or raised elsewhere. Exact gestation/pollination mechanics, litter sizes, offspring survival, maternal mass balance, milk volumes and age to maturity OPEN, as are user's other pending species features. Earlier assistant trial using elephant-like single calf reproduction must be marked superseded by this **preferred design direction**, not presented as settled reality. Owning reference: [01 World and Shimmer](01_World_and_Shimmer.md); full handoff in economy repository.

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Starspawn flesh disappears after Recall; nutritional assimilation persists

**Final ruling for material persistence:** When the Astral Heart begins Celestial Recall (ordinarily about **24 hours after death**), **unassimilated Starspawn flesh disappears regardless of butchering, separation, cooking, refrigeration, Wakecraft freezing, transport or storage**. **Nutrients/managmins already digested and biologically assimilated by another creature persist**; Recall does not reverse meals. The physical threshold for completed assimilation remains OPEN. Remote settlements generally move **living Starspawn** to local slaughter and promptly eat/prepare the meat rather than storing carcasses indefinitely. This supersedes all earlier proposals for permanently retaining butchered pieces.

**Plant salvage:** Red-managmin plants are generally **carnivorous** as a botanical design direction. Carnivorous plant digestion of meat nearing spoilage/Recall may preserve some assimilated material/managmins in new biomass, but conversion is **lossy**; exact percentages, species, speed, plant care and market role remain OPEN. **Nutritional direction:** flesh is a significant source of red managmins, hard to fully replace from ordinary foods, but not yet an approved quantitative species food-managmin table. **Meat must remain a dietary and social staple** in Canopy rather than become inaccessible luxury. Relative target: ~**twice as scarce and no more than four times as expensive compared to an as-yet unspecified real-world/historical reference**; exact benchmark, price units and regional comparisons OPEN. Owner: [World and Shimmer](01_World_and_Shimmer.md#immortality-and-celestial-recall); companion economy studies updated separately.

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Starspawn Recall delay, reappearance, pain and Canopy meat-ranch culture

**LATEST PRECEDENCE:** Fatal Starspawn bodies ordinarily remain for approximately **24 hours before Celestial Recall begins**, superseding older text suggesting immediate Recall upon ordinary complete destruction. The author gives **~8 hours without refrigeration** as practical meat spoilage concern, not a universal precise safe-consumption time. Once Recall begins, established Astral Heart matter reclamation remains. A Starspawn earnestly seeking return to Mystaria may accomplish it in **about a season**, while one content in the Celestial Realm may be absent **a year or centuries**. The Celestial Realm is an effectively **infinite spatial plane** with most Starspawn living there and continuous births; its fearsome predators help motivate emigration to Mystaria. On return, Starspawn have lost **most fat reserves and some muscle**, requiring feeding and recovery. Most experience dying, and particularly being eaten, as horrific, retaining lasting memory rather than treating immortality as immunity to suffering.

**Canopy husbandry:** Starspawn supplying **renewable/nonfatal ingredients** are highly prized. Stock primarily valued for **flesh** often suffers strict, spartan, highly secured confinement that neglects its personhood. Giant aggressive or magical livestock (e.g. triceratops-scale or fire-breathing) can cause disastrous ranch breakouts; dangerous forest-floor ranches need defense, and hunting replacement stock is a culturally significant activity. **Unresolved**: meat persistence after Recall starts, especially detached/processed/consumed flesh; slaughter consent and exact laws; instant Recall for exceptional obliteration; return location, retrieval, individual reconstruction and exact mechanical durations. A 24-hour initiation delay DOES NOT establish infinite preserved meat. See [01 World and Shimmer](01_World_and_Shimmer.md#immortality-and-celestial-recall).

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR CORRECTION: Transmogrified uses 2× Power buildup, not 2× MP; helpless puddle and 5% lost mass

**Supersedes the immediately earlier Rank III living-target `2× spell-equivalent MP` surcharge.** A legal Reshaping III + Vital Transmutation living state-change is a **pure status attack** applying **2× eligible ordinary spell Power as Transmogrified buildup**, with **no extra twofold mana cost**. Do not double the state effect a second time to invent 4× status Power. Existing thresholds **1× SR = one PP; 4× SR = immediately incapacitated/liquid or gas** remain. Casting costs, anchoring, defenses, actual target contact and Hex still apply.

**Helpless transformation and permanent physical loss:** Once fully transformed into a puddle/gas the target is helpless; opponents can divide, bottle and physically carry transformed portions. On loss of supporting magic, separated eligible portions attract together for only **six seconds** and only with force allowed by the spell's actual Power; blocked/unrejoined pieces leave actual permanent deficits. **About 5% of the original transformed creature's material missing on reformation is enough for one wound.** This is not permission to target an arm or vital organ: removed material is an undifferentiated portion. Larger loss may cause further wounds or irrecoverable reformation failure, with no approved additional percentages or automatic injury ladder. Burned/chemically transformed pieces do not rejoin. Original 2×-MP rule is SUPERSEDED; all other Reshaping ranks remain.

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Reshaping I Tempering, II Articulation and State Mastery reformation

**Complete rank progression:** **0 Fundamental Transmutation**, **I Tempering** (anchored supernatural hardening/softening; ½ spell Power structural Defense rider remains proposed for testing), **II Articulation** (sustained caster-directed motion of reshaped matter, not independent Autonomy), **III State Mastery**, **IV Magnify/Minimize**, **V Philosopher**. User explicitly approves original Rank I/II concepts; former Rank I/II unselected status superseded.

**State-shift reformation:** Once a temporary Rank III changed-state anchor stops supporting its effect, **remaining eligible separated pieces attract together with finite force based on the original spell's applicable Power for no more than SIX SECONDS**; afterward the resulting form/completeness is permanent without magical continued attraction. A master's tiny stone droplet might penetrate a building where a novice's would be stopped. Genuine chemical conversion or burning away means the lost/altered material is **not** drawn back. Minor missing material leaves real missing pieces; major shortages can injure the original object/creature or defeat reformation. Controlled removal of shifted portions may enable efficient industrial processing, without granting free missing matter or approved factory output numbers. Applies equally to **living beings** lawfully state-shifted using Vital Transmutation.

**Drinking stone turned into water:** On loss of the anchor, drinker faces an **Opposed Check, Endurance resisting the reformation spell's Power**; failure **Stuns for ONE ROUND** as eligible stone attempts to leave the body. The check uses the general relative-statistic Naked-d20 ladder; exact physical wound outcome is not yet specified and no automatic unavoidable kill is granted.

**Advanced living State Mastery:** Human/creature-to-liquid/gas application requires separate learned **Vital Transmutation**, costs **2× the otherwise comparable spell-equivalent MP**, and causes **Transmogrified buildup**: **1× SR one Pressure Point; reaching 4× SR immediately removes target from combat** during its legally supported transformation, with existing status threshold/resistance still mandatory. No free first-hit removal unless buildup legitimately reaches 4×. Exactly which spell components are doubled and detailed anatomical damage/casting timing remain open. Previous author limit of **×2 state-conversion Power only** remains; it does not double later reformation impacts.

**Owner:** `20_Nymbrin_Wetcraft_and_Hexen_Canon.md`. Index updated. Industrial economics remain deferred. No balance simulations performed.

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: State Mastery power scope, volume/mass size steps, Philosopher mass change

**Reshaping III, State Mastery:** The **×2 Power** applies to the actual *state-changing effect*, including eligible target resistance, **not** unrelated consequential damage or all physical follow-on effects. Do not double a liquid surge, collision or ordinary attack merely because the initial state conversion succeeded.

**Reshaping IV, Magnify / Minimize:** The fourfold "size" step is a factor of **4 in both VOLUME and MASS**, **not 4 in each linear dimension**. Normal Minimize -> 1/4 volume and 1/4 mass; normal Magnify -> 4× volume and 4× mass; each further fourfold step requires ×4 the preceding step's effective Power. The anchored transformation remains temporary, retaining actual reversion damage and constraints already approved. Exact treatment of altered/detached portions remains open.

**Reshaping V, Philosopher:** May change the target's **mass** as part of temporary material identity transformation; **volume tends to remain consistent** while mass changes with target material density. This is a specific high-rank, anchor-dependent exception to normal material constituent/mass exchange, requiring a **somewhat similar** valid source and the usual legal Power and access. Iron->adamantite and milk->wine allowed; trufula->adamantite and motor-oil->wine disallowed. No perpetual material or permanent matter creation from temporary Philosopher. Detailed consumption, shape and heterogeneous-material handling open.

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR-SELECTED RESHAPING III–V: State Mastery, Magnify/Minimize, Philosopher

**Rank III State Mastery supersedes prior rank-III proposals.** Alchemist can shape **liquids/gases** and temporarily change matter's state (solid/liquid/gas), with **×2 eligible spell-effect Power** for changing physical state. Such state changes require active **anchor sigils** and revert to original state on loss of anchor/duration without upkeep. Living-target changes require legitimate **Vital Transmutation**, building a new **Transmogrified** status: at **1× applicable SR one Pressure Point**; at **4× temporarily removed from combat** while supported. Eligible buildup and resistance formula, consequences of reversion, contact, and status-rider exact operation remain OPEN.

**Rank IV Magnify/Minimize:** Anchored temporary alterations in target **size/volume/mass**, including creatures only with living alchemy. Ordinary reduction is **4× smaller**, with each further fourfold change requiring **4× additional Power**. Enlargement likewise permitted; its exact geometric factors, mass origin and proportional Power schedule not yet fully stated. Reversion from an anchor/duration can cause actual harmful expansion, author-specified **ordinary base casting Power damage**, with DM authority for extraordinary situational multipliers (e.g. cramped chambers or ingested size-changing water). No invented multiplier, guaranteed-kill effect or ignore-all-defense rule; collision/resistance/exchange details OPEN.

**Rank V Philosopher:** Anchored temporary change of an eligible material into a **somewhat similar, valid material** for comparable Power, with more permissive temporary material substitution than Recomposition, but not unlimited arbitrary cross-type conversions. Author-approved examples: milk->wine and iron->adamantite are possible, motor oil->wine and trufula->adamantite are not. With legitimate Vital Transmutation, may **temporarily polymorph one creature into another entire creature**. Anchor/duration loss restores original material/form subject to lawful real-world consequences. Exact equivalence, high-grade material handling, creature stats/abilities, magical soul/celestial identity, engineered Quality and damage interactions OPEN.

**Precedence:** These specific author-selected ranks replace earlier proposal choices III–V; no new approved choices for I/II have been supplied. All earlier approved Rank 0, spell MP/Power, Magnitude, anchoring, Hex and material resistance constraints remain outside explicit exceptions. Owner `20_Nymbrin_Wetcraft_and_Hexen_Canon.md`; index updated. No simulations.

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Opposed checks, 9+ critical failures and circle-hacking security

**General mechanic:** A new universal **Opposed Check** compares relevant defender/attacker statistics and resolves via the same six Naked-d20 ratio-based category ladder already used for Combat Speed hit/evasion; it is **one category-based d20**, not necessarily both sides rolling. The current defensive/attacking ratio bands are `<.20` Certain, `.20–<.80` Easy 4+, `.80–<1.25` Average 8+, `1.25–<2.50` Hard 12+, `2.50–<5` Very Hard 17+, `>=5` Impossible. For numeric failed rolls `failure margin = target number - rolled number`. **Failure by 9 or more is now called critical failure**. This terminology does not impose arbitrary universal harm; each use determines consequences. Use this as a backbone for future skills/medium-seizure integration while respecting separately approved prior specialized rules until formally reconciled.

**Circle security:** Hacker must have learned **Autonomy III Reactivity**, testing their applicable effective INT against the circle maker's creation-time effective INT on the general opposed framework. Failure **1–4** allows another lawful attempt; failure **5–8** denies access for **10 minutes**; failure **9+** triggers any applicable alarms and denies access for **24 hours**. The previously specified 9–12 band is extended to all 9+ critical failures; no alarm is created if none exists. Successful intrusion does not bypass circuit throughput, reach, mana, prerequisites or environmental losses. Identify future security permissions, duration of hacked access and other details as OPEN.

**Capacity and entropy:** Round computed **fractional Channel Limits/circle throughput DOWN**. New Haze IV 25% / V 50% mana loss acts as an **additional independent modifier**, not an arithmetic sum of cooperative and weekly ritual losses that nullifies assistants' contributions. Preserve 100 ally MP -> 50 cooperative -> 25 week-long -> 12.5 in Haze V before final integer rounding. Local heterogeneous Haze, exact modifier sequencing and other fractional accounting still need review.

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Haze channel entropy and alchemical circle capacity/interoperability

**Ambient channel entropy:** In **Haze IV**, **25% of channeled mana is lost to entropy**; **Haze V loses 50%**. Haze 0–III have no added loss from this specific rule. Determine effective delivered mana *before* checking the spell's minimum effective MP requirement. Spending enough raw mana to compensate is possible only inside actual Channel Limit, action/ritual capacity and resource constraints. A 10-MP effect with full one-turn CL 14 succeeds at Haze IV (14×.75=10.5 effective), but fails at Haze V (14×.5=7; 20 raw required). Approved prior cooperative/weekly ritual entropies still apply independently; exact compound ordering and rounding remain OPEN. These losses explain **operational circle failure** in Haze IV/V without demanding the physical circle be destroyed.

**Circle construction throughput:** A circle's rated throughput cannot exceed its maker's applicable Channel Limit **at construction time**, including legitimate **ritual multipliers** if produced through a lawful ritual. Larger installations thus need skilled/ritual construction; subsequent users cannot automatically raise a circle's installed capacity. Effective usage also respects their own actual CL and current environmental loss.

**Interoperability:** Hostile/other alchemists may use another's unprotected circles by default, but unfamiliar circle styles yield **half effective installed circle channeling capacity**, not half the user's personal CL/Power. After **ten minutes of communication and style alignment**, cooperating alchemists may use each other's circles at full ordinary capacity. **Autonomy III Reactivity** may be used to create circles with user-specific authorization/rejection, an important industrial security feature. Exact security contest, tuning scope, environment/link losses, action/time costs and integer rounding OPEN.

**Owner:** `20_Nymbrin_Wetcraft_and_Hexen_Canon.md`; index updated. Older Haze lore describing circle failure without a mechanism is qualified by this approved capacity/entropy explanation.

## November 21, 2026 — HAZE TIERS AND PURITY ALCHEMY: Author direction takes precedence (numeric calibration OPEN)

**Approved qualitative hierarchy:** Environmental Haze uses levels **0 through V**; 0 normal clean regions, I outskirts and nearby foreign borders, II ordinary pollution, III hazardous industrial smog, IV critical exposure with vulnerable creatures collapsing and exposed alchemical-circle failures, V unbreathable saturated air requiring sheltered alchemy. This tier framework **takes precedence over incompatible older atmospheric descriptions**, preserving earlier explicit Scarlands life-expectancy, outsider clearbreath and Starspawn vulnerability lore where compatible.

**Hexed inhalation exposure:** Use the existing Hexed status rather than creating another status. Baseline exposure buildup Power approximates a **level-10 Nymbrin with an implement, half earned allocated points in INT, and no extra offensive MP**; calibrated neutral-implement equation `(INT10^2+IR^2)*0.55`, exact initial Nymbrin INT/implement and damage rates OPEN. Exposure scales upward with Haze level, recommended initial **experimental** I–V multipliers 0.5/1/2/4/8 times that baseline. **Clean-air breathing clears 10% of applicable Hex Status Resistance in buildup per complete turn**, subject to universal 1×/4× severity thresholds.

**Purification:** Leywell-powered alchemical **clearbreath masks** with purifying sigils reduce the wearer's effective environmental Haze by **two tiers** while powered. **Purity Circles** are an extra-cheap alchemical anchored operation with **two free duration tiers**, reducing up to two levels of local Haze in their lawful working area, subject to appropriate energy and anchor infrastructure. Vital Transmutation may permit a living-alchemy purge of a target's Hexed buildup **into the environment** and separate increased lung resistance. Precise costs, interval, status-buildup amount, purified-pollution destination, duration-tier rules, prevention of recursive free self-purification, and spell ranks remain OPEN. No battle simulation was performed. Updated owning canon and index.

## November 21, 2026 — NYMBRIN: Hex-capacity short-rest casting, Sigil Scar cleansing, and civic Circuits (AUTHOR-SELECTED TEST DIRECTIONS)

**Casting design selected for balance testing:** Ordinary spell-equivalent cost `M` remains the Channel Limit/Power/Magnitude measure; Nymbrin Wetcraft uses **3M personal Hex rather than spending personal blue MP**, against a personal Hex capacity equal to **maximum personal MP**. Cannot exceed the capacity. A **10-minute rest** releases stored Hex for free to the alchemist, **not** to the environment: environmental Hex remains real pollution. Thus ordinary between-rest spell-equivalent budget is `floor((maximum MP - current personal Hex)/3)`, also bound by Channel Limit and all other conditions. No actual simulation, minimum-reserve exception or fully ratified external-source/ritual interaction yet.

**Scar healing decision:** Willing target can remove **pre-activation buildup** or an active Sigil Scar with healing magic whose eligible Power matches/exceeds **original scar spell Power**, accepting Toxicity. **Approved scar-removal Toxicity is +20 percentage points per scar removed**, including preactivation buildup; actual wounds healed are charged their separately approved **+20 percentage points per wound**. Scar lowers only **END-derived physical Defense**, with a floor of **1**, leaving armor's separately derived protection intact. Preserve 1×/4× severity, 2× casting-Power dedicated application and provisional half-Power rider pending balance testing.

**Circuit worldbuilding direction:** Long chains of large relay/**antenna** circles may reach cities and dependent settlements, transmit real blue mana, and maintain distant alchemical anchors. Mining foundations or housing are potential applications. This is not authorization to erase Hex pollution through a circuit or create mana from nowhere. Link losses, sources, authorization, durability and civic scale remain OPEN.

## November 21, 2026 — NYMBRIN WETCRAFT: Author-selected Circuit and Sigil Scar directions (numerical balance pending)

**Author direction:** Call linked circles a **Circuit**, and distinguish a circle's interior working area from its **Extended Range** for legal placement/links. Magnitude allows larger circles, not blanket increased circle manipulation reach. A caster in reach of a connected circle can operate through a legal Circuit, including supplying real blue mana to accessible distant anchored sigils. Lower-Magnitude circles may establish the next-higher category in **one action** at lawful placement reach, generating Hex; multiple circles can chain. Huge circles specialize in large operations but can deploy smaller circles within lawful domain. Connected physical material can extend manipulation only to that circle's Extended Range, losing active control when severed, without erasing stabilized matter.

**Anchor principles:** Anchor scale tracks affected scale, with an intended two-category allowance (candidate formula `max(0, effect magnitude - 2)`). Anchors exist on the altered matter, require appropriate spell Duration, inherit their substrate's normal unbuffed durability, and cannot themselves be magically hardened. Refresh by paying the original full spell MP again in real blue mana through a lawful Circuit connection. Hardening and softening are anchored physical-Defense riders; **half Power** is a **working test proposal**, **quarter Power** an alternative, not finalized canon.

**Sigil Scar direction:** An unnatural living-material alteration may leave an anchored visible circle scar and work as a two-severity status at **1× and 4× applicable resistance**. Scar application has dedicated **2× eligible casting Power** buildup, not automatic buildup on every alchemical attack. Physical Defense debuff scales upward at Severity II; exact coefficients remain OPEN. Removal requires appropriate scar-bearing tissue removal or healing Power at least equal to the original scar-producing spell Power; magical scar removal produces Toxicity. Retain already-approved **+20 percentage points per actual wound healed**; additional scar-only Toxicity still needs a decision. No automatic erasure of stable Hexen mutation.

**Still open:** Physical circle dimensions; distance/link geometry and scaling; circle material/counterplay; timing/MP for circuits; scar resistance and defense interface; debuff coefficients, anchoring Duration/renewal execution; Hex production, release and environmental accumulation. No simulated balance claims. Source owner: `20_Nymbrin_Wetcraft_and_Hexen_Canon.md`.

## November 21, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Physical stability alone controls Nymbrin transmutation persistence (LATEST)

**APPROVED MODEL B, with explicit choice of physical stability alone:** When a lawful Wetcraft transmutation leaves a physically viable finished material arrangement, that arrangement **persists** without a surviving circle, ongoing magic, additional stabilization stage, or mastery-dependent separate permanence purchase. If the altered configuration would not remain physically stable, it **depends on a functioning anchoring circle** for continued alteration; breaking the anchor removes that support, allowing lawful physical reversion/settling, never infinite force, restored destroyed matter, or reversal of intervening events.

**Preserved:** Nymbrin modern equivalent exchange (weight, feedstocks/constituents and complexity), hard protective material resistance, all-alchemy-produces-Hex, and separate Warlock temporary Blue Morph/reversion including mold-assisted mundane production. Nymbrin permanence does **not** provide free repairs without missing components, automatic ore-to-masterwork conversion, Quality V gear, bypassed smithcraft/forge requirements, continuous magical work without resources, or unrestricted industrial production.

**NOT APPROVED BY THIS DECISION:** Numeric Hex generation or natural dissipation, gloves/circle dimensions and reach, preparation timing, circle durability, anchor maintenance/force, rank-specific techniques, MP/SP formulas, industrial Pazara circuit enhancements, species rarity, or new economic production rates. These are future design subjects. Updated subject owner: `20_Nymbrin_Wetcraft_and_Hexen_Canon.md`; navigation: `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md`.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR CORRECTION: Boss XP one level; encounter-equivalent quest rewards (LATEST)

**APPROVED: Boss XP is now exactly ONE guaranteed level advancement**, measured at the Hero's level and existing XP progress when the Boss is overcome. With current Hero level `L` and progress `P` toward level `L+1` (`0 ≤ P < L×(L+1)`), award **`Boss XP = L×(L+1) − P`**. Hero becomes level `L+1` with zero progress toward `L+2`. Example: level-50 Hero at 500/2,550 progress earns 2,050 Boss XP and reaches level 51. This special Boss reward replaces, rather than adds to, normal enemy-level XP. The former exactly **TWO** guaranteed level-ups and additional `[(L+1)×(L+2)]` Boss XP are **SUPERSEDED**. All normal per-level XP requirements, non-Boss threat values, patron award qualification, stats and progression remain as approved.

**APPROVED: flexible encounter-equivalent quest valuation.** A DM may determine the XP and Gem value of qualifying quests, investigations, rescues, peaceful solutions and combat-bypassing deeds by estimating roughly **how many qualifying monsters / equivalent encounters and of what difficulty** the deed warrants. This may be estimated during preparation or **retroactively on completion**. Do not require kills; keep the patron's existing authority to deem deeds eligible. Avoid rewarding the same resolution twice by automatically combining its full combat reward and full bypass-equivalent reward. There is **no required percentage split** between encounter and quest payouts and no newly approved numerical quest multiplier.

**Currency and Gem boundary:** Existing denomination remains **100 Glints = 1 Gem**; only whole Glints are paid, with any smaller theoretical remainder deferred or qualifying rewards bundled. Approved Boss **Gem** rewards currently remain **two levels of reference budget**, `E(L+2)−E(L)` within the existing defined range, because the author's correction explicitly changed **Boss XP** only. The mismatch between Boss one-level XP and two-level Gem reward is **open for a future explicit choice**. No numeric monster Gem chart, mandatory rounding method, smoothed replacement reserve, or fixed encounter/quest split is approved by this entry.

**Files updated:** `01_World_and_Shimmer.md` (owning XP / quest mechanic), `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md` (Boss XP cross-reference and quest Gem guidance), `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md` (current precedence), `10_Canon_Changelog.md` (this record). ## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Offensive MP-to-Power chart, ten-minute ritual ×4 capacity, structural Defense tiers (LATEST)

**CURRENT APPROVED OFFENSIVE POWER BENCHMARK:** For ordinary offensive spell Power, the author explicitly approves the MP-investment multiplier ladder previously used for the castle calculations. At neutral implement tuning, the approved working equation is `Power_offense = (effective governing attribute² + eligible implement rating²) × M(nominal MP assigned to base offensive Power)`; for the Kharak Pyromancy reference the governing attribute is effective **INT**. The implement Rating (IR) is a separate additive squared equipment contribution, **not** a weapon-style multiplier on INT. All existing implement-specialization rules remain, including Offense tuning modifying **only implement-derived Power**, one chosen implement per spell, resource and medium requirements, and special spell/form exceptions. Do not transfer this ordinary offensive Power formula automatically to healing, purely utility, non-damaging status abilities or other techniques with separate approved mechanics.

| Base offensive Power MP | Approved multiplier |
|---:|---:|
| 0 (legal offensive cantrip) | ×0.55 |
| 1 | ×1.00 |
| 2 | ×1.35 |
| 4 | ×1.70 |
| 8 | ×2.05 |
| 12 | ×2.25 |
| 20 | ×2.51 |

**20 MP remains the maximum for the unmodified base offensive Power component**, excluding separately payable magnitude/area, duration and other legal spell modifications. Spell Power may NOT be treated as unlimited by channeling more base offensive MP beyond 20; any extra legitimate MP must finance other legal priced components, unless a separately approved exception applies. The exact curve/interpolation for MP values **between listed points** and rounding of fractional final Power/MP payment are still OPEN; do not invent extra multiplier steps or assume free interpolation. Cantrips retain normal spell/medium/range/channel restrictions and the at-most-one-offensive-attack-per-turn rule.

**APPROVED TEN-MINUTE RITUAL CHANNEL CAPACITY:** A legal **10-minute ritual** may channel up to **4 × the caster's applicable full Channel Limit (CL)** into one working, subject independently to the caster's **actually available MP**, valid replenishment/contributions, spell prerequisites, medium, legal costs, interruption, duration, magnitude/area and other restrictions. This is a **capacity multiplier**, not a free Power multiplier, MP discount, extra mana source, or automatic entitlement to affect a whole castle. Earlier progression choices of **two-turn ×2 full CL** and **one-minute ×3 full CL (the latter a previously designated interpretation)** remain; longer-duration channel-capacity math is still not numerically finalized. **Short rituals provide no automatic personal mana regeneration**. Experimental Mastery schedules of 0/3/6/9/12/15 at the tested levels and the precise overall `CL=floor(effective INT/10 + Mastery)` expression remain **unapproved calibration fixtures** unless independently finalized in the owning rules.

**APPROVED STANDARD STRUCTURAL DEFENSE TIERS:** For reference mundane objects/structures use the following **structural Defense Power** thresholds (not physical armor AR or standalone MR values):

| Reference material / construction | Approved structural Defense Power | Intended specialized offensive caster breakthrough benchmark |
|---|---:|---|
| Ordinary wood, ordinary wooden doors and planks | **1,000** | About level 1 |
| Thick timber and thin stone | **8,000** | About level 25 |
| Ordinary unenchanted castle masonry | **12,500** | About level 50 |
| Reinforced stone and substantial structural metal | **40,000** | About level 75 |
| Extreme mundane nonmagical fortifications | **80,000** | About level 100 |

All **five** values above are author-approved, including the four that were provisional in the preceding November 20 castle calibration record. The qualitative progression targets are **benchmarks**, not automatic permission to bypass armor, spells, wards, unique divine/magical materials, attack legality or physical reach/coverage. A 'breakthrough' in the initial numerical calibration means overcoming the first meaningful wound threshold on the part actually reached; a person-sized through-hole or total collapse still depends on **attack coverage, structural geometry, thickness, injury interpretation and target area**. A spell legally covering and damaging an entire castle may wound the whole as one target; one covering only the door wounds only the door, per prior approved rule. Warriors with sufficiently powerful, legitimately delivered attacks can wound the same structures without requiring spellcasting; ritual scaling is a separate caster advantage.

**PRECEDENCE AND LIMITS:** This entry explicitly supersedes descriptions of these **four non-castle structural Defense values**, the **listed MP multipliers**, the **neutral-implement offensive-power formula**, and the **10-minute ×4 CL capacity** as 'experimental', 'proposed', or 'not yet canon' in the immediately preceding structural-calibration entry and older spell-rules notes. It does NOT approve the specific example Kharak caster's Mastery purchases, historical Blank/Mixed attribute-enchantment legality, numerical spell Magnitude/area or structural-through-thickness criteria, specific attack hit probabilities, or Combat Lab structural/ritual support. Prior manual comparisons were arithmetic fixtures, not measured simulator outcomes.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Castle Defense 12,500 and structural breakthrough benchmarks (LATEST)

**APPROVED:** The ordinary unenchanted castle-masonry **structural Defense Power baseline is 12,500** for the current wound-based structural calibration (instead of the earlier proposed 17,000 or 13,225). This is a structure-defense reference benchmark, **not** an automatic Boughsteel armor AR/MR rating or a universal rating for every castle architecture or enchanted fortification. Apply existing wound/impact ratios provisionally when benchmarking structures; actual affected scope still follows the previously approved rule that only the area the attack can cover and damage is wounded.

**Author-selected progression targets:** A reasonably specialized **level-1** offensive caster should be able to penetrate ordinary wood; about **level 25** should penetrate thick wood or thin stone; about **level 50** should consistently inflict meaningful wound damage to ordinary castle masonry without having to rely on a ritual; about **level 75** should penetrate substantial/reinforced stone or metal; by **level 100**, a suitably developed caster should penetrate the upper end of ordinary nonmagical material/fortification defenses. This last design goal does not override specifically resistant divine, unique, or enchanted materials. 'Penetrate' in these numerical models means surpassing the first damaging wound threshold **when the attack successfully lands on a legally covered part**; a full through-hole still depends on thickness, scope and structural wound description. Ritually invested attacks can sometimes cross a tier earlier, preserving the previous level-25 small-castle-breach ritual objective.

**Calculated candidate structural-Defense tiers, NOT YET CANON except 12,500 castle:** Ordinary wood/doors **1,000**; thick timber/thin stone **8,000**; castle masonry **12,500 (APPROVED)**; reinforced stone/structural metal **40,000**; extreme nonmagical structures **80,000**. The other four are explicitly **PROPOSALS** pending further confirmation; they are not universal material durability values. These bands were fit to an experimental reference Pyromancer build and must remain independently adjustable for thickness/material, attack type, and magical protection.

**Manual calculation fixture, NOT new canon:** Kharak starting STR22/DEX15/END20/INT17/SPD14, racial +25% INT, all earned allocated points divided evenly into INT and END, every-five-level stat increments, neutral Quality I/I/II/III/IV/V implements with approved IR26/26/30/35/40/48, and working (NOT approved as a final spell law) `P=(effective INT²+IR²) × proposed MP multiplier`. Levels 1/10/25/50/75/100 one-action legal-cost tier investments 1/2/4/8/12/12 MP yield approximate Power **1,128 / 2,566 / 7,151 / 21,013 / 43,102 / 70,209**. Ten-minute ritual experimental capacity and Mastery fixture, capped at 20 MP base offensive investment, yield **2,312 / 4,772 / 10,558 / 25,728 / 48,082 / 78,322** Power. One-action spells respectively first exceed the first wound threshold of proposed Defense tiers 1,000 at level1; 8,000 at level25; approved 12,500 at level50; proposed 40,000 at level75; proposed 80,000 at level100. At level25 a 10-minute ritual can already cause a Solid wound on 12,500-Defense masonry, whereas an ordinary one-action spell cannot; 'about level50 consistently damages castle' refers to ordinary casting against this reference, not immunity to lower-level rituals.

**Critical boundaries:** MP-to-Power multiplier chart (0 MP×0.55, 1×1, 2×1.35, 4×1.70, 8×2.05, 12×2.25, 20×2.51) remains the author's agreed **experimental starting chart, not final canon**. Ten-minute ritual throughput multiplier ×4, illustrative Mastery rank values 0/3/6/9/12/15, gear affordability, and exact area/duration modifier prices remain **UNAPPROVED fixtures**. Do not infer attack success probability, full breaching of thick walls, automatic castle-wide area, normal spell eligibility of every fixture, or Combat Lab simulations. No simulation was run for these structural outputs.

## November 20, 2026 — APPROVED ELEMENTAL STATUS RESISTANCE FORMULA (LATEST)

**Author-approved formula for each applicable elemental status type:**

```text
Elemental SR = ceil( ((effective END + 0.65 × applicable MR)^2 × ER_element) / 0.70 )
```

Here **effective END** includes qualifying equipment bonuses and normal effective-attribute effects; **applicable MR** means the legal Magic Resistance for the relevant target/status context, subject to existing armor coverage, named materials, exceptions and separate defenses; **ER_element** is the *applicable existing named element-specific resistance multiplier* (use **1** where none applies). Do not invent a new ER source or assume a numerical ER value for an unresolved material. **Ceiling is applied once at the end** of the calculation, not separately to MR weighting, the squared term, or the elemental multiplier. MR coefficient **0.65** and divisor **0.70** are now explicitly **CANON**, superseding older 'unapproved typed SR equation' notices. This replaces the older standalone **SR = effective END²** calculation for *elemental typed statuses*; retain that earlier value only where a distinct rule specifically calls for END² outside this elemental-SR procedure.

**Normal legal elemental contact contributes 100% of its eligible delivered elemental Power to the matching status buildup**, without the old universal ×0.70 offense coefficient. Maintain the existing actual-contact, interception, medium, power, magnitude, three-turn same-element accumulation/refresh, and element-specific resistance rules. **Do not equate buildup to final injury stages or physical weapon damage**: use the actual eligible *elemental* Power reaching the status-delivery step. Direct-injury Power/damage and other spell damage calculations are not automatically multiplied by 1/0.70 or changed by this status-only normalization. Do not remove independent status application requirements, defenses, or specific elemental effects.

**Preserve attack-form exceptions relative to the new 100% ordinary buildup:** Ordinary Fire **100%**, Blue Flame **50%**, White Flame **0% and no refresh**; Wakecraft's dedicated no-damage Freeze Attack **200%** of otherwise equivalent eligible Freeze magnitude; other established spell, enchantment or status-specific adjustments apply only when already canonically defined. Applicable thresholds remain **0.5×, 1×, and 4× elemental SR** with element-specific exceptions (including Ice's separately defined 12× Entombed threshold); this update does not change severity outcomes, tick cadence, durations or any previously approved attack costs.

**Rationale and balance boundary:** Algebraically relocates the experimental 70% ordinary elemental-buildup coefficient into the precomputed defensive threshold: `Power×0.70 / OldSR = Power / (OldSR/0.70)`, apart from final rounding. E.g., effective END **50**, MR **40**, ER **1** gives `ceil((50+0.65×40)^2/0.70) = 8,252`, and a lawful elemental Power **3,000** adds **3,000** ordinary buildup. The current combat simulations were performed under their recorded historical experimental policies; **no post-approval balance rerun or simulator engine migration is claimed**. This is not a blanket approval of an independent formula for Psycraft/mental or other non-elemental status systems; their previously approved procedures remain. Interaction of Water's percentage MR erosion with recalculating ongoing typed SR and other previously open timing/rounding interactions remains **UNRESOLVED**.

**Precedence:** Any older sections here or in `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md`, `10_Canon_Changelog.md`, or `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md` saying the 0.65 MR weighting, typed elemental SR combination, or universal 0.70 elemental coefficient are 'unapproved' or that elemental SR uses END² alone are **SUPERSEDED** by this entry. Other historic approvals (elemental weapon Power I–VI, three-flame penetration, Wakecraft forms and status effects) stand.

## November 20, 2026 — THREE-FLAME PYROMANCY APPROVED (LATEST)

**AUTHOR-APPROVED CANON:** Pyromancers have three offensive flame forms: **Ordinary Fire**, **Blue Flame**, and **White Flame**. Ordinary Fire bypasses **0%** of armor-derived Magic Resistance (MR) and delivers **100%** of ordinary eligible Burning buildup; Blue Flame bypasses **25%** of armor-derived MR and delivers **50%** of the same Burning buildup; White Flame bypasses **50%** of armor-derived MR and delivers **0%** Burning buildup and **does not refresh** an existing Burning pool. All modes use the ordinary spell's legal Power, accuracy, MP/medium/channel/action costs, and other existing defenses; penetration affects the **armor-derived MR component of direct magical injury defense**, not independent MR, shields, wards, physical AR, or whole-body ongoing Burning status resistance. The three-flame choice and current **adaptive flame selection** are accepted gameplay behavior. The precise adaptive scoring heuristic is a Combat Lab implementation, not a newly imposed universal player decision rule.

**AUTHOR-ACCEPTED MATCHUP BALANCE:** Pyromancers are strongly favored against ordinary Boughsteel opposition (author's ~**85%** benchmark), strongly disadvantaged against Nullporcelain (author's ~**10%** Pyromancer / **90%** Nullporcelain benchmark), and Glassweave is an intentional anti-magic counter with the earlier approximately **40%** Pyromancer target. These percentages are **balance expectations, not automatic combat outcomes or universal statistical guarantees**. Observed conditional level-25 fixtures: Boughsteel Light adaptive **78.4%** (500 encounters); Glassweave Heavy adaptive **44.4%** (500); Nullporcelain Heavy with **declared, accessible** weak points and precision targeting adaptive **10.0%** (400), versus **0%** when no precision targeting was enabled (500). Fixtures used seed 42, experimental spell-damage/status-resistance policies, and unverified full build/equipment parity. Do not assume every Nullporcelain suit has accessible gaps; precise gap attacks incur the applicable accuracy tradeoff. This **supersedes** earlier changelog/index/subject notes saying Blue/White MR bypass percentages and White Flame mechanics are unapproved; it retains the older 50%-Blue-Burning approval.

**Scope:** This approval settles the three flame forms and their above numerical attack differences, not unapproved universal typed-SR equations, character progression/wealth parity, new spell prices or an altered physical Ice Stab rule.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Spell coverage determines structural wound target scope (LATEST)

**Approved area-to-wound targeting rule:** An attack that can **legally encompass an entire structure** and has **sufficient applicable damage to harm that entire structure** may treat the **entire structure as one wound target** and resolve its wound against the whole. If the attack legally encompasses **only a particular part** (for example, a castle door), **only that part receives the wound**. Attack area/coverage and ability to cause damage are separate requirements; large area alone does not guarantee penetrating structure resistance. This supersedes any universal requirement that castles must always be segmented into independent wall/pillar/gate wound records. Subsections are used only when the attack's scope or its effects are actually localized.

**Benchmark request, pending numeric implementation:** Compare **level 1, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100** Pyromancers each making a **ten-minute ritual**, with **at least 50% of earned attribute allocation points invested in INT and END collectively**, against an unenchanted castle wall calibrated as the **Boughsteel-like structural baseline** (a reference/tuning intent, not an approved value of wall AR or MR). Consider a novice capable of damaging a mundane wooden door even when stone fortifications remain safe. A ten-minute ritual's numerical channel throughput, Power-versus-MP scaling, ability to obtain/spend sufficient mana, caster build details and the castle material's physical/magical defenses are still open. The current Combat Lab interface supports duels and comparative spellcasting experiments, **not structural targets, ten-minute rituals, or whole-castle wounds**; do not present six-level structural results as measured until suitable supported simulation runs succeed. Existing qualitative siege progression targets remain design benchmarks.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR DIRECTION: Object/structure wound model and martial–magical siege parity (LATEST)

**Author-selected design foundation:** **Most non-fragile items and structures should use the existing wound-based damage/severity system**, not generic independent HP pools. The wound framework's exponential/nonlinear nature should permit substantial ranges of structural outcomes, from negligible damage through breaches to catastrophic destruction. Fragile objects can retain simpler breakage methods where appropriate. **Precise object material defenses, structure-specific wound interpretation, geometry, collapse, sectioning, thresholds, and multi-hit persistence are not yet numerically calibrated**; do not invent them as approved.

**Comparable Power, comparable potential:** If a warrior's lawful attack is comparable in applicable physical Power to a mage's lawful attack against a structure, the warrior should be able to damage/breach it through the common wound system as well, subject to the structure's actual physical versus magical resistance, attack form/contact and material. Castle stone is **not immune to mundane weapons merely because it is stone**, and damage equivalence is not automatic if resistances, area or attack delivery differ. The fundamental difference is access to **spell rituals** that let casters invest more energy and apply effects at larger scales; warriors do not automatically acquire equivalent magical ritual throughput.

**Castle design targets, not finalized numbers:** Very-low-level Pyromancers cannot meaningfully burn through ordinary unenchanted castle masonry; lower-mid-level Pyromancers can create a person-sized breach through a ritual; mid-level Pyromancers can create a large breach through a ritual; high-level Pyromancers can breach in a single spell and can destroy an unprotected castle down to its foundations with a sufficiently powerful ritual. The terms 'level' here are qualitative; no exact levels, MP prices, wall-resistance values, breach dimensions, or ritual times have been approved. Ordinary stone need not literally combust; applicable Pyromancy may break it through magical heat/thermal fracture or pressure, subject to designed mechanics.

**Pending implementation proposal, NOT canon:** Represent a castle as meaningful targeted sections (gate, wall, pillar, tower) with separate wound results and possible support-triggered collapse. This avoids requiring one attack to destroy the whole structure when it only affected a person-sized patch, but exact section resolution/structural support and spillover rules await selection. Preserve the existing wound categories and material-specific AR/MR interactions until their structure adaptation is explicitly approved.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Encourage INT² potency is current canon (LATEST)

**APPROVED:** The nonmagical **Encourage** action reduces eligible emotional/mental magical status buildup by the **encourager's INT² for two actions**, or **half that magnitude for one action (INT²/2)**. This is now the canon working numeric formula rather than an unapproved proposal. **Spellcasting implements do not modify the amount.** The speaker must be within **30 feet** of the affected ally, the ally must **hear the spoken encouragement**, and a **strong personal relationship** must exist; strangers and comrades with no meaningful connection do not qualify. No mana is spent. The mechanic is deliberately less specialized than dedicated Psychic intervention, and stronger for INT-investing magical characters than many warriors. Balance may be revisited by explicit future approval, but do not present the existing formula as provisional meanwhile.

**Resolution:** Apply the resulting reduction using the approved universal active-status rule: if buildup falls **below 4× resistance**, Severity II drops to Severity I; below **1× resistance**, the condition ends, including when the original duration was extended or permanent. An eligible loss of the status that made a target Finisher-eligible can interrupt a pending Finisher. The formula does not permit encouraging away nonemotional statuses, does not confer a spellcasting implement benefit, and does not bypass relationship/hearing/range restrictions. Rounding for odd INT²/2 values and edge cases concerning multiple speakers or ambiguous relationships remain OPEN; do not invent different numerical scaling.

**Precedence:** Supersedes the November 20 Encourage design note describing INT²/INT²÷2 as PROVISIONAL. The future Dispel Potion remains an unpriced, undeveloped item concept.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Universal active-status reduction and severity downgrade (LATEST)

**Approved universal rule:** Any legal **status-buildup reduction** affects the **currently active status immediately**, not merely buildup for an untriggered future application. Across **all statuses**, lowering the target's remaining buildup **below the 4× resistance threshold** downgrades an active **Severity II** condition to **Severity I**; lowering buildup **below 1× resistance** ends the active condition entirely. At or above 4×, Severity II remains; at or above 1× and below 4×, Severity I remains. This applies regardless of whether the status was originally produced by a normal-duration, extended-duration, or permanent spell. Long duration does **not** make a status immune to sufficient buildup reduction. The effect is a threshold downgrade/removal, **not an automatic restoration of the caster's prior buildup when the duration continues**.

**Examples:** Reduce active 4× Charm beneath 4×: control/allegiance override ceases, leaving only the lesser 1× suggestibility and source-specific penalty while eligible buildup remains. Reduce beneath 1×: Charm ends. The same two-tier threshold logic applies to other status conditions, including those reduced by Wakecraft Cleanse, nonmagical Encourage where eligible, and a future Dispel Potion once that item is developed. For future Dispel Potion, the potion's actual amount and price are **not yet approved**; for Encourage, the **INT²** reduction values remain a **provisional** proposal.

**Boundary:** This decision does not supply a new source of status reduction or waive its action, range, relationship, medium, magical-resistance, cost, or legality rules. Other future reapplication, subsequent buildup, and expiry timing rules are not invented here. This entry supersedes the prior statement that interaction of status reduction with active conditions was unresolved.

**Future Dispel Potion (DESIGN NOTE, NOT A FINISHED ITEM):** Add a potion concept that **reduces buildup from all magical status conditions**, rather than only one chosen category. Potency, cost, crafting, availability, action/draw/drink economy, Toxicity, interaction with ordinary magical effects versus statuses, and activated-condition removal are OPEN. It operates at **up to 30 feet** and requires the recipient to **hear the speaker**. Mere membership on the same side is insufficient: two soldiers who do not even know each other's names do not qualify. The intended use includes rescuing a beloved ally under an extended or even permanent Charm effect, even when the controlling Psychic/charmer is far away. This is a proposal the author framed as 'likely,' not a rigorously balanced or expressly finalized numeric approval. Rounding, effective-versus-natural INT, simultaneous encouragement, total status-reduction floor, resistance, and scaling remain OPEN.

**Critical interface still OPEN:** Existing status rules allow release at 1× or 4×; whether an already-activated status retains reducible buildup, how lowering buildup downgrades/ends an active effect, and how this interacts with the Charm duration refresh and paid permanent/extended durations have not been specified. Do not automatically assume an activated status is cancelled as soon as its historical buildup falls below an activation threshold. ## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Finisher interruption, Charm refresh, modular status duration (LATEST)

**FINISHER INTERRUPTIONS (APPROVED):** An announced physical Finisher still costs **two actions**, must be performed from **within 5 feet**, has **×4 damage rather than automatic death**, and resolves **at the start of the attacker's next turn**. Before resolution, the Finisher is interrupted if **(a)** the intended victim **ceases to be an eligible target** (for instance, awakening from Sleep, ending qualifying immobilization, or losing the Severity II / 4× Charm that supplied eligibility), or **(b)** the attacker **can no longer complete the attack** (for example, target moved out of required range or attacker disarmed). A mere hit on the preparing attacker does **not** automatically interrupt absent a real loss of qualification or attack feasibility. No new guaranteed-hit or defense-bypass mechanic is conferred. Other specific feasibility disputes follow ordinary action/positioning rules, not invented auto-interrupt triggers.

**CHARM DURATION (APPROVED):** Both **Severity I / 1× Charm** (subtle friendliness/suggestibility and charmer-specific combat penalties) and **Severity II / 4× Charm** (genuine allegiance change and competent hostile fighting) have a **base duration of three rounds**. **Applying additional Charm status refreshes the active Charm duration**. Precise timing if refreshing with a lower-severity application, and whether ongoing accumulation versus actual applied status counts as refresh, are left to general status application rules where specified; do not silently promote a 1× Charm to 4× without the required status threshold. Existing breaking conditions remain: attacks by the charmer or the charmer's allies break Charm **after the attack resolves**, at either severity. Severity I Charm remains **ineligible** for physical Finishers; Severity II qualifies.

**MODULAR STATUS DURATION (APPROVED):** **All statuses** can have their duration changed through the universal **modular spell Duration option**, **provided that the final triggering spell** has legally paid the extra duration price. Earlier buildup hits do not pay that price on behalf of the triggering spell, and extra buildup by itself does not constitute free extended duration. Status severity thresholds (1× / 4× for the mental-control examples), required magical Power, effect eligibility, normal defenses, Channel Limit, legal casting, duration-modifier price status, and specific exceptions remain unchanged unless explicitly revised. Exact numerical duration modifiers/cost ladder remain as previously marked (some provisional), not newly approved here.

**PRECEDENCE:** This entry resolves prior open Charm base duration and Finisher interruption criteria in the November 20 Psychic/status entries; supersedes the words describing Charm duration or Finisher interruption as wholly open. No combat simulator results are claimed.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR DECISION: Psychic emotional control, subtle Cipherlight, and physical Finishers (LATEST)

**Status:** Author-selected mechanics. Earlier exploratory four-stage (1× to 4×) emotional-control duration interpolation is superseded by the existing **two-severity thresholds at 1× and 2× status buildup**. Emotional effects accumulate via attacks; the attacker chooses whether to continue buildup or release it, including on the same attack that increases it. An overwhelmingly powerful attacker can therefore activate a weak victim's condition immediately, subject to normal resistance. The exact decay of unreleased buildup, interaction with other conditions, and extra MP to extend duration remain OPEN.

**Confusion:** Severity I lasts **1 round**, Severity II **3 rounds**; severity changes duration, not the D3 procedure. When the affected creature attacks, casts a spell, or makes an analogous qualifying action, roll **D3**: **1** = Psychic chooses a valid target other than the creature's intended target, potentially exploiting the confusion; if no valid alternative exists, action fails harmlessly or fires in a useless direction. **2** = action wasted. **3** = action resolves as intended. This also affects beneficial spells/actions when qualifying; exact boundaries for non-targeted or area effects are OPEN.

**Anger:** Severity I **1 round**, Severity II **3 rounds**. Affected creature attacks the nearest creature other than itself; eligible offensive spells may be used when it can take an action. Ties, inability to attack, and action selection remain OPEN.

**Fear:** Severity I **1 round**, Severity II **3 rounds**. Affected creature retreats from the source as quickly as possible, using its actions to dash or magical movement when possible; if cornered, cowers without acting. Appropriate movement spells are permitted. Exact path selection, source disappearance and what counts as cornered remain OPEN.

**Charm (advanced):** Status application uses **half the attacker's normal applicable magical Power** (not half the result after successful application). At Severity I, the victim is suggestible, generally regards the charmer as a friend outside combat, and in combat suffers **−2 accuracy and −20% attack Power only when attacking the charmer**, not the charmer's allies. This lesser charm is subtle: a typical victim does not believe they were charmed. At Severity II, the victim **switches sides** and fights sincerely and competently for the charmer, without deliberate self-sabotage or suicidal action; it is not permission to deliberately remove oneself from battle through ineffective choices. Victims remember their actions afterward. **Either severity breaks if the charmer OR one of the charmer's allies attacks the victim, only AFTER the provoking attack has resolved**. Precise Charm duration, control hierarchy, and noncombat behavioral boundaries remain OPEN.

**Sleep (advanced):** Status application uses **half normal applicable magical Power**. Severity I puts victim to sleep for **up to 3 rounds**, Severity II for **up to 1 minute**. A creature wakes if shaken or struck; an ally can spend **one action** to wake them, or use a qualifying ranged attack or spell to wake them. Sleep itself is not automatic death, and normal attack/Finisher/Execute legality remains relevant. Trivial versus damaging spell contact, environment and timing of awakening remain OPEN.

**Subtle Psycraft Cipherlight:** All Psychics must have a way to deliver appropriate hypnosis/mental influences **unobtrusively outside combat**, by **taking longer rather than spending more mana**. It does not waive a suitable mandatory focusing gem or existing Cipherlight delivery, resistance and contest restrictions. Exact additional time and detection procedure remain OPEN.

**Physical Finishers:** Separate from magical instant-kill **Executes**. A Finisher takes **two actions**, is available to physical and magical characters, requires the attacker to be **within 5 feet of the target**, and deals **×4 damage** when resolved, **not automatic instant death**. It resolves **at the start of the attacker's NEXT turn**, creating a window for interruption. Creatures affected by **Charm, Sleep, or immobilization** are eligible targets. Whether either Charm severity alone suffices, which immobilizations count, what preserves or interrupts a declared Finisher, exact attack/damage timing, armor/defense interaction, and whether eligibility is rechecked at resolution remain OPEN. Do not silently add an automatic success or bypass ordinary defenses.

**Priority integration:** Psycraft, universal status buildup, magical contests, and combat action timing should reference these rulings; exact numeric status Power formula is still in calibration. This is not an approval of a combat-simulator implementation or test result.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: Mana potion catalogue, Toxicity implementation, extra refill doses and obsolete shop warning (LATEST)

**Approved offensive-price correction:** the provisional base offensive spell investment ladder now reads **0 MP cantrip; 1 MP basic; 2 MP enhanced; 4 MP strong; 8 MP greater; 12 MP superior; 20 MP maximum**, before area, duration or additional modifiers. The author-selected price benchmarks are retained as the **current WIP ladder**, not a verified final spell-Power-per-MP formula; the previous 11 MP superior and 18 MP maximum proposals are superseded.

**Approved Toxicity treatment:** rename Heal Burn to **Toxicity** throughout current usage. Toxicity can accrue from healing, mana restoration and other explicitly eligible effects. Using **maximum usable MP after Soul Strain** as the denominator, drinking a mana potion grants Toxicity equal to **100% × actual MP restored / current usable maximum MP**, with excess potion restoration wasted once MP is full. Toxicity is cumulative. At **100%** a recipient has a total of **1 Toxicity wound**, at **150%** total **2 wounds**, at **200%** total **3**, then one more total wound every additional 50 percentage points. Wounds are **threshold-based totals**, not added again each time a potion is consumed while already above a threshold; effects and wounds caused by reaching thresholds cannot be healed until rest permits it. Exact rest-based Toxicity reduction and release from wound-healing lock are still OPEN. Keep the preexisting per-injury healing-Toxicity percentage benchmarks pending a full healing cost review.

**Approved tiered mana-restoration potion proposal, now baseline for continued calibration:** One ordinary drink restores **Tier I (level ~10): 5 MP at 6 Gems; II (~25): 10 MP at 12 Gems; III (~50): 20 MP at 24 Gems; IV (~75): 40 MP at 48 Gems; V (~100): 80 MP at 96 Gems**. Effective potion restoration is capped at usable missing MP. The comparable **one-dose-per-day refillable** prices are **60 / 120 / 240 / 480 / 960 Gems**, respectively. At a given tier, each extra daily drink/charge on a refillable adds **50% of the tier's base refillable price**, repeatedly, with no numeric maximum count yet selected. Thus an item with N daily doses costs **base × [1 + 0.5 × (N−1)]**, before any as-yet-unapproved modifiers; each dose is a separate potion drinking/use opportunity. Replenishes **one use per daily charge**; additional purchased charges each also refill once per day. Refillable potion terminology, contents/vessel and interactions with rest or day boundaries remain to detail. The approximate 1:10 disposable-to-refillable price relationship and current economy references remain. Do not assume potions are manufactured or ubiquitous without crafting/availability rules.

**Approved use and threat:** Drawing a potion costs **one action**; drinking costs **one action**; drawing during a grapple needs a **Technique check** (numerical check and outcomes TBD). Eligible enemy prepared attacks or grapples can interrupt access or destroy the potion via ordinary legal interaction; no free reaction or extra attacks. Mana potions restore actual MP without changing maximum MP. Toxicity is shared with healing and future expressly eligible buffs, making replenishment trade off against injury treatment.

**Critical source-quality warning:** The old **'Consumables — Early Stock' Gem Shop inventory** in `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md` (including old **20-Gem Mana Dew** and healing vial offers) is **OUTDATED / NOT A CURRENT PRICING REFERENCE**. It must be comprehensively revised before used for offers, economic comparisons, or future consumable balancing. Preserve historical records but never treat that catalogue as authoritative current market pricing. The present tiered potion reference and latest 3,200-Gem level-100 equipment portfolio, 30%-of-lifetime-earnings consumable allocation take priority.

**OPEN:** Healing-potion potency/toxicity pricing integration; short-rest / long-rest Toxicity clearing and treatment of threshold wounds; mana potion sourcing, alchemical craft requirements, inventory and cost materials; potion usability by zero-natural-MP Warlocks; crafting of permanent daily-refill vessels; refill trigger timing and stacking; precise MP-to-Power conversion; updated skill-specific spell costs; marginal price/value effect of MP cost-modifying implements.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR APPROVAL: 20-MP offensive benchmark and Toxicity resource-potion design (LATEST)

**Offensive spell investment, author-selected WIP design:** revise earlier **Greater** benchmark to **8 MP**, retain **Superior 11 MP**, and set **maximum unmodified base-effect/Power investment at 20 MP**, before duration, area, and other spell modifiers. Retain previously discussed basic 1, enhanced 2, strong 4, and 0-MP cantrip as **working ladder**, not a fully calibrated/approved MP-to-Power equation. Actual impact of additional mana on Spell Power and any overall price multiplier remain under testing.

**Rename:** The former **Heal Burn** mechanic is now **Toxicity**. Toxicity is a shared drawback accrued from relevant restorative effects, including healing and new mana-restoration potions, and potentially later potion buffs/other specified effects. This is a new balance subsystem rather than a blanket grant of potions/crafting ranks.

**Author-directed Toxicity thresholds:** accumulated Toxicity reaches harmful wound territory at approximately **100%**, with **1 wound at 100%, 2 wounds at 150% and +1 wound at each additional 50 percentage points** (200%→3, 250%→4, etc.). These Toxicity wounds **cannot be healed until the recipient rests**. The speaker also said 'once you exceed 100%'; the exact boundary wording is ambiguous and requires confirmation; **100% inclusive** is the working reading of the explicit 'at 100%, it's 1 wound' example. Existing Heal Burn's prior approved per-injury percentage schedule (superficial 5%, first ordinary injury 20%, first Guard 10%, next Guard 15%, etc.) is preserved **as a starting Toxicity accrual schedule**, pending a review of how healing and potions share the meter. Short rest/long rest Toxicity reduction amounts and how temporary wound locks lift remain to be integrated; do not invent cures or permanent recovery impairment.

**Soul Strain interaction:** for percentage-based Toxicity calculations, treat **maximum usable MP after Soul Strain** as the character's maximum mana, not the hypothetical unstrained natural reserve. Numerical mana restoration/Toxicity conversion is not yet approved. Avoid assuming Toxicity automatically lowers maximum MP, or that existing Soul Strain was removed.

**Mana potions and action economy:** Mana-restoring consumables are intended to restore actual spendable MP (up to the user's usable maximum). The user approves a tactical sequence requiring **one action to draw a potion and one action to drink it**; enemies can exploit legal prepared attacks on the potion or interfere with the user. **Drawing an item during a grapple requires a Technique check**, with its exact difficulty and opposed-resolution mechanics pending. This rule does not create additional attacks or waive reaction legality.

**Pricing direction:** propose tier-appropriate single-use mana potions priced at **roughly one-tenth of a full comparable item** of the tier, and **once-per-day replenishing/refillable potions** costing as much as the full comparable item. Use the **current** approved tenfold-redominated economic framework: level 10/25/50/75/100 primary item reference costs **60/120/240/480/960 Gems**, endgame wealth **3,200 Gems**, and consumables **30% of lifetime gross earnings (~2,014 Gems through level 100)**. Specific mana restoration values, tier potion prices, Toxicity-per-restored-MP equation, refillable daily charge count, exact potion availability and crafting are **PROPOSALS pending approval**. The older 20-Gem 'Mana Dew' shop offer requires reconciliation, not silent deletion.

**Other unresolved design issues:** immunity to healing above the Toxicity limit, how lasting/rest-locked wounds interact with preexisting injury states, blood/liver toxicity remedies, Nymbrin potion manufacturing and recipes, action interruption, whether unused healing/potion strength creates Toxicity, and handling of Warlocks' zero natural MP/external reserves.

## November 20, 2026 — AUTHOR DECISION: Craft Mastery points and universal pool; offensive MP ladder under review (LATEST)

**Approved Mastery gain:** Each magical Craft has **20 Craft-specific upgrades** and **20 non-specific/universal upgrades** in the intended modular progression. Each purchased Craft-specific upgrade grants **0.5 Mastery points for that Craft**; each purchased non-specific/universal upgrade grants **0.25 Universal Mastery points**, applying to relevant Crafts. **Round down the final combined Mastery** (not individual fractional gains). Full investment grants **10 craft-specific + 5 universal = 15 Mastery maximum** for a Craft. Expressed as `Mastery(c) = floor(0.5 × craft_specific_upgrades(c) + 0.25 × universal_upgrades)`. Universal Mastery is one shared pool and is not repeatedly counted for the same Craft.

**Channel Limit integration:** Previous author direction sets the INT-derived component at **half its former weight, with the former −10 INT offset removed**, plus the separate automatically accumulated Craft Mastery. A natural **working formula, still awaiting numeric calibration/explicit ratification**, is `CL(c) = floor(effective_INT/10 + Mastery(c))`. The Mastery accrual and cap are approved; the combined formula's precise rounding, minimum CL, edge cases and calibration are NOT yet final. Do not revert to the legacy `ceil(max(1, INT−10)/5)` formula without recognizing supersession direction.

**Offensive pricing review, NOT approved:** The author recalls a possible ~18 MP maximum for unmodified base spell Power and is considering an MP-cost multiplier and future mana potions. Current GitHub records do **not** establish an approved general 18 MP offensive price ladder. Candidate comparison ladder: cantrip 0, ordinary basic attack 1, scalable stronger single-target attacks **2 / 4 / 7 / 11 / 18 MP**, excluding area, duration and specialized modifiers. These are **assistant proposals only**, not final canon. Exact MP-to-Power function, whether 18 is a ceiling or a reference investment, combat balance, high-level casting, and any future mana potion mechanics or availability remain OPEN. Do not invent an approved potion.
