## November 18, 2026 — New accumulated Elemental Magnitude and END-derived Status Resistance (FRAMEWORK APPROVAL)

**Author's redesign:** Elemental Magnitude is now the amount of **elemental Power that actually contacts and reaches a target**, accumulating in a **three-turn elemental condition** each time that kind of elemental attack makes legal contact. New universal **Status Resistance scales with END**. The approved equation is in the later entry above. Fire: under **0.5 SR** smoldering does nothing; **at least 0.5 SR** one meaningful self-PP; **above SR** ongoing burning damage; **at least 4 SR** twice normal burning damage. Mundane and magical acts can cleanse or intensify this condition, including water/oil and conductive metal with lightning. Earlier SPD ignition, separate END severity test, perpetual burn-until-put-out as an uncapped default, Smoldering inherent Fire Resistance decrease, and generic Contact Factor are superseded. Preserve genuine contact, existing medium, armor and shield rules, five-round Leywell enchantment activation, tier VI Mana Blade, two-action economy and peer-level parity targets.

**Historical calibration:** The former Fire Power proposal was 204/421/955/1705/2671/6678 for I–VI. The new Tier I–V values supersede the first five entries. The last value remains a Tier VI proposal. See the [Modular Equipment draft](24_Modular_Equipment_Design_Options_DRAFT.md).

## November 18, 2026 — Remove generic Contact Factor and record historical SPD ignition and END intensity

**Approved corrections:** **Discard Contact Factor completely as a generic elemental calculation**; do not multiply elemental Power/Magnitude by the old fire-metal ×1.25, insulation ×0.5 or any other global delivery multiplier. Genuine heat/energy pathways, struck shields/barriers, material properties, insulation and separately established specific Elemental Resistance still apply normally and should not be double counted. **Lightning** may receive its **own bonus against real conductive metal armor** where the shock actually reaches the wearer, but the bonus value/conditions remain for separate design.

**Burning Edge uses distinct defensive jobs:** On legal elemental contact **SPD determines chance to ignite**; once ignition succeeds, **END and appropriate Fire Resistance determine fire intensity and injury severity**, not SPD. A burning effect then persists until genuinely extinguished or deprived of fuel, **without repeated SPD/END checks to set its duration or intensity**. Slower targets ignite more easily, but their burn duration is not currently determined by an automatic SPD timer. **Smoldering** is the fallback when the target ignites but resists fire injury, delivering one meaningful self-PP and a modest fire-only Resistance reduction; the exact percent is still OPEN. Keep tiers I–V peer-relative effectiveness, the Tier VI Mana Blade exception, real media and approved Leywell costs unchanged. Old numerical Flaming Edge/Contact Factor proposals remain historical and unapproved. ## November 18, 2026 — Enchantment resource identities and item interactions (LATEST AUTHOR APPROVAL)

**Enchantment modes ratified:** Blank = continuous full stat boost paid through Soul Strain, Mixed = continuous smaller stat boost paid through Soul Strain **plus** Leywell-powered effect with **no extra Soul Strain**, Full = **no stat boost** and a Leywell-powered magical effect **one effect tier higher**, with no active-effect Soul Strain. Existing Quality I–V stat reference values are retained. Full effects use the **same normal MP cost as their actual higher tier**, not an additional multiplier. **Tier VI effect** at QV Full is conceptually approved: **one simple magical effect with base output on par with a moderate specialist operating at their peak**, but very few activations from a normal maximum **Tier V 50-MP Leywell**. Do not grant the specialist's complete Craft, new item Quality or Leywell Tier VI. Exact VI effect/MP numbers remain unresolved. Continuous stat bonuses do **not** require five-round MP reactivation; activated effects continue to use Leywells and their own timing. [Owning equipment entry](09_Equipment_and_Economy.md).

**General interaction rules approved:** Retrieving accessible items or interacting with the physical world (e.g. opening a door) costs **one combat action**. One action can draw or sheathe **up to two weapons**. Exception: with a free hand or a hand freed from a two-handed weapon, **one readied thrown weapon carried in a bandolier/quiver may be drawn and thrown in one action**, counting against the existing one offensive attack-action limit. Swapping equipped rings or other gear requires actual interaction actions; a carried cache of offensive magical rings cannot be instantly cycled for free and does not increase the approved two active ring positions. Exact full-slot ring remove/replace action count remains unresolved, as do unapproved individual Tier VI activation costs. [Combat reference](22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md).

**Latest author direction:** Establish **Blank** (stats only), **Mixed** (moderate stats + normal magical effect), and **Full** (no stats + distinctly stronger effect) as the three equipment-enchantment modes. Keep historic Quality I–V stat benchmarks: Pure **+6/+12/+20/+28/+36** as the Blank reference, Mixed **+3/+6/+10/+14/+18** as the Mixed reference. The author favors **Full magical effects one tier above Mixed**, mapping QI–V items to effect tiers II–VI instead of I–V. ## November 18, 2026 — Secretly prepared active enchanted defense (AUTHOR APPROVED)

**Active defensive enchantments follow the existing prepared defensive-action model (Parry and applicable prepared magical defenses), not an on-demand free reaction.** On the defender's own turn, **secretly commit the required one or two combat actions**, identify the specific equipped defensive enchantment, and declare a **narrow, legal, outcome-independent trigger** in advance. The prepared enchantment takes effect at its lawful response opportunity if that trigger occurs and all requirements (including appropriate Leywell power, physical medium where relevant, and ordinary positioning/eligibility) hold. The defender cannot wait to see whether the attack would hit or deal damage before choosing the trigger or defense.

**Examples:** “The next attack against this named ally” or “the next attack made by this specified enemy” may qualify when the item actually supports that coverage. “The next attack that hits me” is not eligible as an outcome-dependent trigger. Follow the already approved preparation/expiry and relevant action limitations of the defensive framework being used; no additional defensive action, free attack, or reserved action beyond the existing two-action economy is created. Magical defense mechanics are not automatically granted the Parry-specific +1/+2 hit category, Pressure Point rewards, cooldown, or shield routing unless the individual enchantment explicitly earns such behavior under its actual approved rules.

**Distinction preserved:** Action-free passive modifications of an existing defense (e.g., an eligible preactivated reinforcement effect) remain passive; an enchantment that **independently performs an active defensive maneuver** consumes the preparatory action(s) and obeys the secret-condition system. The five-round duration of ordinary magical enhancements is distinct from the time window of a prepared, triggered active defense. Further item-specific duration on activation, expenditure timing if a trigger never occurs, trigger expiry, response scheduling, multiple prepared effects and coordination with the single prepared spell constraint require explicit calibration. They are **not** authorization for unlimited simultaneous active defensive reactions.

## November 18, 2026 — Passive versus active enchantment action economy (AUTHOR APPROVED)

**Classification by behavior, not simply by whether magical energy is spent:** An enchantment that merely **modifies a legal action or enables a new capability** is a *passive/modifying activation* and **costs zero combat actions to switch on**, even when it consumes Leywell MP and maintains a time-limited magical effect. Examples include igniting a sword, boosting movement speed, or enabling an alternate mode of movement without actually moving the user. A character may activate **as many eligible passive/modifying enchantments as desired during their own turn**, subject to actual installed items, sufficient correctly colored Leywell mana, necessary real media, ordinary eligibility and any separately approved restrictions; no universal one-passive-per-turn cap.

**Independent actions:** An enchanted item that **actually performs an action the user would normally spend actions on**, including moving the wielder, launching its own attack, or actively defending, requires **one or two combat actions** according to the effect's design. These active uses must respect the existing **two-action turn and maximum one offensive attack action**; a magically produced attack is not an extra free strike merely because an item creates it. The exact 1-versus-2 action assignment remains for individual enchantments.

**Durations:** Previously approved ordinary enchantment activation lasts **five combat rounds** unless an explicit item rule provides an exception. Action-free activation does **not** mean MP-free activation. Independent actions and sustained modifying effects still consume their relevant Leywell MP according to applicable costs.

**Timing and interruption questions OPEN:** Resolve whether an **ordinary spell in the act of casting or channeling can be interrupted by damage**, and if so which damage events qualify, whether a check is required, what happens to paid MP and partially completed actions, and which separately approved exceptions survive. **Use that spellcasting decision as a reference before deciding whether damage similarly interrupts the existing two-action Leywell-recharge operation.** Do not assume all damage automatically cancels charging, or that it can never interrupt charging. Active enchanted defenses also require future integration with prepared defensive spell timing, turn windows and existing reaction/action constraints. None of these unresolved questions alters existing specific Shocked or anti-magic interruption effects.

## November 18, 2026 — Leywell charging action, rounding, and five-round enchantment activation (AUTHOR APPROVED)

**Transfer accounting:** A legitimate contributor spends their own MP of the Leywell's exact matching color. Apply the approved **90% transfer efficiency** and **round the amount actually deposited DOWN to whole MP** after calculating the transferred amount; never round each constituent point up. Thus 10 MP spent → 9 stored, while 5 MP spent → 4 stored. Charging cannot exceed the Leywell's maximum (Tier I–V capacities **10/20/30/40/50 MP**) or the contributor's available MP. Fractional transfer yield is lost, not retained as partial MP. The contributor bears the actual spent MP cost, even when the destination fills before all theoretical yield would fit; efficient contributors may choose the amount transferred.

**In-combat recharge timing:** Charging a Leywell takes **two combat actions (approximately six seconds of real-world time)**. This is an action cost for a charging operation, not two additional mana charges or an automatic mana-generation process. The amount actually chargeable in one operation is bounded by available compatible MP, 90% efficiency rounded down, and remaining Leywell capacity; no additional fixed per-action transfer cap is approved here. The physical access, interruption and out-of-combat procedural details remain open.

**Ordinary enchantment activation:** **Most enchanted-item effects activate without spending a combat action**, and each normal activation lasts **five combat rounds**. The effect uses its Leywell for its applicable activation MP cost. An enchantment's explicit exception can have different timing only where separately approved; activation is not a free independent offensive attack or a license to exceed established action/effect limitations. Do not infer unlimited stacking or a free extra strike. Whether repeated activation refreshes the duration, and exact simultaneous activation limits, remain open.

**Approved working enchantment activation-cost ladder (user accepted preceding proposal):**

| Leywell tier | Minor effect MP | Standard effect MP | Powerful effect MP |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| I | 1 | 2 | 4 |
| II | 1 | 3 | 5 |
| III | 2 | 4 | 7 |
| IV | 2 | 5 | 10 |
| V | 3 | 6 | 12 |

These are general **initial design bands**, not an automatic cost or power assignment to every effect; individual enchantments still need compatible color, accessible medium where relevant, and actual effect design/testing. Previous assistant-suggested ten-round duration is superseded by five rounds. Existing exceptional material equipment effects (e.g. Skyvein's approved 6 MP per powered turn) remain under their owning specific rules unless expressly revised.

## November 18, 2026 — Leywell direct-MP recharge, fixed efficiency and five-tier capacity (AUTHOR APPROVED)

**Latest author correction supersedes earlier devotional recharge:** Charging a Leywell **spends the contributing character's own actual MP**. It is **not** an independent mana-generating prayer process, does not create free MP, and does not depend on sincerity, faith, or devotional enthusiasm. Transfer efficiency is a flat **90% for every contributor**, independent of belief: a transfer of 10 MP from a legal source deposits 9 MP, with 1 MP lost. The precise accounting of fractional MP deposits and partial transfers remains open, so no further rounding rule is inferred.

**Strict color identity:** Each Leywell is bound to **one mana color**. It **only accepts transferred mana of exactly that matching color**; e.g., a blue Leywell cannot accept red mana. It does not transmute colors. The contributor must actually have spendable mana of the required color; an affinity alone is not free mana.

**Approved Leywell capacity by tier:** Tier **I = 10 MP, II = 20 MP, III = 30 MP, IV = 40 MP, V = 50 MP**, maximum stored amount. These are Leywell tiers, not automatic character-level grants. No Leywell may be charged above capacity. The former proposed 4/8/16/28/40 reservoir capacities, prior speculative 8/16/32/48/64 ladder, END-linked prayer charging and 10%-efficient reluctant-prayer rule are superseded.

**Duration-first enchantments approved:** Most installed enchantments should operate **for a defined duration after activation**, rather than requiring a new mana payment per hit or individual contact. Their magical power still comes from their appropriate Leywell and their outward effects still require real physical media where applicable. Exact duration, upkeep, per-effect MP cost, simultaneous effect handling, and activation action rules remain to be approved.

**Mundane media maintenance direction:** Elemental enchantments using ordinary fuel/water should consume **extremely small** physical quantities, with practical refueling after roughly **one day of heavy combat or a week of lighter skirmishes**. Fuel is common and easy to replenish (e.g., lantern oil or water). Its physical presence and sabotage vulnerability remain meaningful, but it is the mana supply that does most of the work. The cadence is the author's approved design direction, not finalized per-activation volume, a universal clock or new purchased supply tariff.

**Not yet approved:** Assistant-proposed minor/standard/powerful Tier I–V activation-cost ladder **1/1/2/2/3**, **2/3/4/5/6**, **4/5/7/10/12** MP respectively; tentative sustained-combat duration of up to ten turns; exact transfer-rounding rules; charging time and any charging action constraints. Do not treat these numbers as canon.

## November 18, 2026 — Enchantment philosophy, real media, and Glassweave Leywells (AUTHOR APPROVED)

**Author-approved foundation:** Ordinary enchantments are restrained, purpose-built magical engineering, **not** copies of sophisticated racial Craft spells. Enchanted equipment uses existing magical principles and physical media to execute limited, repeatable functions; it does not grant a wearer mastery of Pyromancy, Wakecraft, or another racial Craft, nor reproduce an elaborate craft technique (for example, a Wakecrafter's independently controlled water-dragon attack). Ordinary enchantments may inject mana into real eligible media to cause basic effects, in a manner broadly comparable to the limited medium-directed application of mana by Warlocks; this comparison does **not** grant Warlock powers or bypass other Crafts' prerequisites.

**Intrinsic enchantments and Anvilcraft:** Anvilcraft's established magical material-working and alteration furnish enchantment's distinctive intrinsic expression. A smith may further alter an item's own properties by enchantment along lines consistent with what Anvilcraft already accomplishes, such as additional magical lightening of a Trufula weapon, without gaining unrelated racial Craft abilities. The scope, magnitude, costs, and precise eligibility of individual intrinsic enchantments remain to be designed; do not infer unrestricted matter transformation.

**Real-medium rule:** Spectacular outward effects must honor genuine medium requirements. An enchanted flaming weapon is not an eternally burning immaterial spell-flame. The author's approved **flaming sword engineering concept** uses (1) a very thin, minimal coating of stored flammable oil dispensed by the weapon, (2) ignition through a tiny **Hearthiron wick**, and (3) mana supplied by an activated **Leywell** to make the established flame burn substantially hotter. The weapon needs **both physical fuel/medium and mana** for its enhanced flaming effect. Its fuel reservoir is a legitimate sabotage or depletion vulnerability; the Leywell is considerably more resilient. This is an approved qualitative construction concept, **not** finalized oil consumption, reservoir capacity, ignition frequency, elemental magnitude, MP draw, or wound mechanics. Other outward enchantments likewise cannot invent required media by merely relabeling their effect as intrinsic.

**Leywell physical form (approved clarification):** Leywells are **not little vials of liquid mana**. They are usually polished **Glassweave orbs or Glassweave cut gemstones**, whose glow visibly communicates the power held within. Their stored magical energy is not a liquid. Preserve existing alternate names *well* and *faithwell*, and already approved capacity/activation rules where separately defined. 'Usually' does not forbid rare exceptional designs; no new universal toughness, price, charging rate, or storage capacity is established here.

**Power source and implements:** Ordinary enchantments **always draw their operating magical power from Leywells**; do not assume they can directly burn the wearer's natural mana reserves or work solely because the wearer has the matching mana color. Future **casting implements** may have narrowly specified exceptions after spell design is settled, but they are specialized **Craft-specific** tools, not universal enchantments usable by anyone with the correct mana color. Do not finalize such exceptions now.

**Preservation and scope:** Established magical colors, medium dependencies, Anvilcraft/Smithcraft prerequisites, physical material effects, Soul Strain rules, and prior approved Leywell-powered mechanisms remain in force. Prior speculative rune/gem-slot counts, active enchantment MP costs, named enchantment families, and catalogue quotas remain **unapproved** until separately authorized. This entry records philosophy and the flaming-weapon example, not a fully calibrated enchantment catalogue.

## November 16, 2026 — Reach distances and Technique-based movement control APPROVED (LATEST)

**Explicit author approval:** Short/Medium melee weapons control only the **1-tile (5-ft)** zone, while Long weapons control only the **2-tile (10-ft)** zone, **not adjacent squares**. Distinguish **attack reach** from **movement control**: Short attacks at 1 tile; Medium attacks at 1 normally or 2 with **one harder hit category** from lunging; Long attacks at 1 or 2 with no innate range-category penalty. A ready, credible defender can require a **Technique movement contest** when an opponent crosses out of its controlled zone, and a Long wielder can contest **entry through its controlled 2-tile barrier into adjacency** by Technique rather than the former SPD thresholds. Success permits lawful continued movement; failure stops at the boundary with no free damage or grapple. Apply **one meaningful strongest-controller contest**, accounting for actual additional threats via existing Pressure principles, without gratuitous multiple checks or unapproved numeric bonuses.

**Explicitly rejected for this change:** automatic grapple on entry, a free/no-action grapple initiation roll, and default attacks of opportunity. Normal grapple initiation remains a committed offensive Technique check under existing action limits. **Superseded:** prior Long-versus-Short 1.25/1.50 effective-SPD reach-control entry gates and old non-distance-defined reach bands. **Unresolved:** exact Technique-ratio d20 bands, Pressure modification to the contest, expenditure/timing and repeated crossing, forced movement and unusual geometry. Do not invent those values. Updated `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md`, `25_Melee_Weapon_Catalogue_DRAFT.md`, `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md`, `10_Canon_Changelog.md`, and `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md`; no WR, attack Power, or armor changes.

## November 16, 2026 — Dash movement-tile multipliers and upward rounding APPROVED (LATEST)

**Explicit author approval:** In the existing two-action physical combat pilot, **Dash (Half Dash, 1 action) increases the character's already determined movement-tile allowance by 50%**, ceil(M × 1.5); **Double Dash (Full Dash, 2 actions) increases it by 100%**, ceil(M × 2), where **M** is the ordinary movement-tile allowance. **Round UP to a whole tile** after the multiplication (for instance, M=5 gives 8 or 10 tiles, respectively). Do **not** re-evaluate SPD-to-tile thresholds or compute extra tiles based on Dash's temporary Combat Speed bonus. Existing **+25%/+50% Combat Speed until the start of the next turn** remains separately operative; initiative, action costs, one-offensive-action limit, reach/terrain restrictions, and other combat mechanics are unchanged.

A valid reach-entry/physical opportunity is required *before* checking for a hold; no two-stage attack-plus-Technique roll, free attack, injury or automatic adjacency grapple is granted. Initiation is an offensive maneuver under the existing **one offensive attack action per turn** constraint. Prior November 16 notes describing Technique initiation as a proposal are **superseded** on this point only.

## November 16, 2026 — Grapple-range combat constraints and escape direction APPROVED IN PRINCIPLE

**Author's explicit direction:** A true grapple denies ordinary Long-reach melee attacks by the opponent; penalizes Medium-reach melee attacks by **one existing hit-difficulty category**; leaves eligible Short melee and unarmed attacks functional; prevents two-handed ranged weapon attacks in the grapple while permitting physically eligible one-handed ranged weapon use; and permits attacks by the grappler to bypass their held opponent's normal shield interception/block (not END or worn armor). **Grapple initiation requires an actual attack check**, not just adjacency. **Grapple escape must be a d20 check favoring combined STR and DEX** and should use existing accuracy categories where feasible. **Failed escape** leaves the character unable to leave the current square by ordinary movement and incurs **one incoming PP**.

**Still pending the author's numerical approval:** Escape ratio/attribute weighting, action costs and legal timing of initiation/escape, failure-PP duration and repeat stacking, and edge cases such as third-party intervention, forced repositioning or special abilities. `STR+DEX` control and `(holder STR+DEX)/(escaper STR+DEX)` mapped to six-category thresholds is an explicitly labeled **test proposal only**. These changes do not approve experimental additive WR or alter approved shield durability/Power.

**Explicit author approval:** Replace the previously approved **+1 harder attack difficulty on Power Attack** with **one self-applied meaningful Pressure Point** lasting **from maneuver initiation until the start of the attacker's next turn**; no inherent Power Attack accuracy penalty remains. Retain **2 actions**, **one offensive attack action**, **×1.25 of otherwise final physical Attack Power**, legal reach/penetration/END/AR/injury calculations and all existing defensive mechanics. **Power Attack is explicitly single-target**, never a free Sweep/Wide Sweep/Line/group attack; it cannot be Quick Attack, Double Strike, or stacked with another offensive attack action. The one self-PP can matter to credible incoming threats according to existing net Pressure tiers; it does not add to the user's offensive Pressure or grant a free counterattack.

## November 15, 2026 — Two-action combat, Naked d20 and Candidate A APPROVED for friends-led physical PILOT

**Author approval:** Adopt the assistant's recommended physical combat package for the author's own unhurried play with friends. **No AI-driven playtests, scheduled follow-up, or obligatory logging.** This is **approved for pilot play**, not proof of permanently completed balancing. The author requested future balancing QUESTIONS only.

**Pilot rules:** **Two actions, maximum one offensive attack action per turn**; Full Attack and approved **60%-per-strike Double Strike** each cost **2**, Quick Attack **1** with **full Power but one harder hit category**, no 80%-Power Quick. Naked d20: **Certain automatic, Easy 4+, Average 8+, Hard 12+, Very Hard 17+, Impossible no ordinary roll**. Keep approved Combat Speed calculation but use **wider pilot cutoffs 0.20/0.80/1.25/2.50/5.00** rather than original **0.50/0.80/1.25/1.50/3.00**. Half/Full Parry **1/2 actions, +1/+2 harder hit categories, 1/2 earned PP for an actually prevented would-be body hit**, with specific prepared triggers, shield-first same-die procedure and expenditure cooldown. Half/Full Dash **1/2 actions, +25%/+50% Combat Speed** through start of next turn, without multiplying movement distance or initiative.

**Candidate A physical shields:** Light/Medium **+1**, Heavy **+2** on legitimately defendable Guard lines. One attack die first tests ordinary baseline, then shielded threshold; **natural miss / shield contact / body hit** are distinct. Supersedes older **automatic physical Guard** and conflicting same-line **+0/+1/+1 obstruction** during the pilot, not established shield durability/overflow, magical interception or material properties. **Deferred questions, not tasks:** low-level wound routes, high-END non-woundability, Heavy shield mirror pacing and wear, material contact-trigger frequency, relative Quick/Full/Double Strike and Parry choices, broader vs original Speed cutoffs, movement/escape/pursuit geometry, shield flanks, magic interface and one-die tabletop usability. The author can revisit these at any time based on actual friend-group play; there is no deadline and no automated combat monitoring.

## November 15, 2026 — DM encounter wound-route check APPROVED; ChatGPT-play priority

**Explicit author approval:** Adopt the early equipment audit's **starter encounter viability check**, and make the requirement **especially explicit for Mystaria played through ChatGPT**. ## November 14, 2026 — Prepared defense expiry and mixed-action rounding approved

**Author decision:** The prepared defense expires at the **beginning of the caster’s next turn**, whether used or unused. Protection beyond that point requires casting a separate spell with sufficient duration or eligible maintenance. The caster names the spell and a specific trigger on their own turn, before the attack outcome is known. “The next attack targeting my knight” qualifies. “The next attack that hits my knight” depends on the outcome and is invalid. The defense draws from capacity reserved on the preparation turn. Future-turn capacity cannot be borrowed.

**Mixed actions:** When otherwise legal normal physical actions and magic are combined, halve the applicable Channel Limit and round down. The caster may make at most one attack total that turn. A Bloomkin may fire a crossbow as that attack and prepare an eligible magical shield for a nearby Thornguard under the normal casting requirements.

**Unresolved:** Exact response timing and priority, mixed-action commitment timing and maneuver qualification, and interactions with complete spell seizure’s prior preparation or next-action forfeiture and other specialist rules.

**Author decision:** On their own turn, casters allocate their existing Channel Limit between any offensive magic and at most **one specific prepared reactive defensive spell**, within the shared budget for all applicable channeling. Name the spell and declare a narrow trigger in advance. The next attack against a specified target or by a specified attacker qualifies. A generic watch for any ally being attacked and any trigger based on an attack's outcome are invalid. When the trigger occurs, activation requires a legitimate response opportunity, the allowance reserved on the caster's own turn, the appropriate physical medium and access, and normal MP payment. A magical shield through a separate eligible caster or powered interface remains conditional on its own approved rules.

## November 14, 2026 — Soul anatomy, casting, and ordinary death

**Author-approved expansion:** [Magic and the Soul](01_World_and_Shimmer.md#magic-and-the-soul) now covers Cognum and memory dispersal, Anima affinity and bodily spellcasting, Spiritus damage and Soul Shred, and the Corpus's role in ordinary death and possible early revival. This expands the earlier four-part anatomy entry. The stomach makes managmins bioavailable to the Anima, and the nervous system and especially the hands support spell shaping. The Spiritus binds the parts and reserves, and structural damage can reduce attributes through Soul Shred. Existing Celestite weapon and armor XP erosion and triggers still apply.

**Ordinary death:** The heart stops, and the loss of the Corpus's protection lets formless black mana contribute to soul unraveling as decomposition sets in. Cognum decay eventually disperses memories. Exceptional early healing may permit revival. Unusual component independence remains possible, including established Cognum preservation during Celestial Recall. The Warlock, Moontouched, and Celestial Recall rulings continue to apply.

**Unresolved:** Revival timing and requirements, conditions for independent survival or function of individual parts, how Cognum persists in Soulwork vessels, and any general Soul Shred procedure beyond established sources. Necromancy remains a future concept involving external mana puppeteering a damaged Spiritus, with mechanics undefined.

Updated [World and Shimmer](01_World_and_Shimmer.md), [Warlock Manacraft](04_Warlock_Manacraft.md), [Centaurs and Smithcraft](07_Centaurs_and_Smithcraft.md), and the [Canon Index](00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md).

## November 14, 2026 — Warlock and Moontouched Anima and Celestial Recall

**Author decision:** Warlocks have the same four soul parts. Their larger, more powerful **Anima** fills the space in the **Spiritus** where pure mana would ordinarily be stored. They need dietary managmins to survive. Their Anima uses trace amounts of mana to move other mana, always less than 1 MP. Warlocks have **0 natural MP** and draw on external mana to use Manacraft. A Moontouched who is not a Warlock has a shriveled, weak **Anima** that digests only enough dietary managmins to keep them alive.

**Celestial Recall:** Once Celestial Recall begins, the **Astral Heart** reaches across the planes and breaks down what remains of the **Anima**, **Spiritus**, and **Corpus**, including the physical body. The **Cognum** remains intact. The Heart combines the recovered material with formless mana to recreate the other three parts and imbues the recreated soul with the original Cognum. Greater damage, greater power, and greater depletion in the original body each increase the mana required and lengthen Recall. Its exact duration is intentionally unspecified. This supersedes the older days-or-weeks estimate.

Earlier descriptions of Warlocks as empty or entirely without mana now apply only to spendable natural MP. Existing Manacraft costs and handling rules still apply. How Warlock soul vessels preserve disembodied consciousness remains open.

Updated [World and Shimmer](01_World_and_Shimmer.md), [Warlock Manacraft](04_Warlock_Manacraft.md), [Races](02_Races.md), and the [Canon Index](00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md).

## November 14, 2026 — Four-part soul anatomy approved

**Author decision:** Anima manipulates and emits magic and converts dietary managmins into pure mana. Cognum is the mind housed in the brain. Spiritus is the stabilized mana framework of the soul and contains pure mana. Corpus is the physical body that anchors Spiritus to this form.

[Magic and the Soul](01_World_and_Shimmer.md#magic-and-the-soul) defines these parts alongside the existing whole-soul description of mana storage and regulation. Existing affinities, racial exceptions, and spell rules continue to apply.

**Unresolved:** How brain-housed Cognum relates to identity and consciousness preserved in a disembodied soul vessel under [Soulwork](04_Warlock_Manacraft.md#rank-v--soulwork), and how the four parts relate to Starspawn Astral Hearts and Celestial Recall. The anatomy of racial exceptions to mana production and shaping is also open.

## November 13, 2026 — Turn-scale Channel Limit and defensive channeling approved

**Historical ruling:** The next-turn borrowing provision below was superseded by the November 14 prepared-defense revision above. The shared throughput and mixed-action rules still apply, with round-down clarified in the November 14 expiry and rounding entry.

**Author decision:** The existing Channel Limit now governs **total channeled mana in a turn**, rather than permitting its full per-effect value repeatedly. A caster can ration offense to retain applicable defensive capacity. After their active turn, permitted defenses may borrow the **next** turn's channeling allowance; mana spent then reduces both their MP reserve and the next turn's remaining channel budget. A caster can be forced onto defense to exhaust next-turn options. These rules do not themselves authorize additional actions, new interrupts, or free repeated reactions.

**Mixed actions:** Characters may combine legal physical actions and spellcasting, but their Channel Limit is **halved** and they can make **at most one attack total in that turn**. Do not stack physical Double Strike or a weapon attack plus a separate offensive spell into two attacks. Existing casting/physical action legality still applies.

**Preservation and open implementation:** Existing attribute-derived Channel Limit formulas, MP/SP costs, class/racial skill ledgers, Wyrmcraft Overchannel/Serpentbreaker and other specialized exceptions, Warlock external-mana/Handling Capacity, physical Guard and attack rules remain unchanged. Still open: exactly when reactive interventions are legal and how they interact with complete spell seizure's action debt, as well as other conditional exceptions. See [Magical Media and Contests](35_Magical_Media_and_Contests.md).

## November 13, 2026 — Magical media and spell-seizure rules approved

The author rejects treating “mastery expands access” as a universal Craft progression, replacing it with **Craft-specific medium dependencies**. Wakecraft requires controlled liquid water; ice/vapor require trained recovery before control and may require a recovery action and Channel Limit. Pyromancy can amplify a match, spend flames as ammunition and seize fire into smoke for specialized techniques. Psycraft uses gem-focused Cipherlight, not abundant-light scaling; closed eyes resist but do not immune, and an established psychic effect can persist across interrupted beam contact while the focus survives.

**Contest thresholds:** one existing spell Power statistic, not separate control: equal Power seizes medium (no additional spell on that turn), double Power seizes spell (prepare by sacrificing prior-turn action or surrender next action). Extra MP committed to challenge is spent, even on failure. Medium seizure uses only one's own compatible Craft, not free enemy abilities. Wakecraft may displace/freeze/vaporize seized water; pyromancers inhale fire to produce specialized smoke; psychics dispel an opposing effect and can bolster a third party's will against enemy mind control. Third-party target resistance persists.

**Supersession with preservation:** older direct ice/vapor Wakecraft control, notably literal Threefold Weave, conflicts with newer liquid-only rule and must be redesigned without silently deleting named ranks or SP costs. Existing Naga Psychokinesis and other approved ranks remain historically preserved pending separate remake. Do not invent detailed timing, MP or Power formula, volumes, or completed pyromancy skills. See [Magical Media and Contests](35_Magical_Media_and_Contests.md).

## November 13, 2026 — Physical ranged benchmarks and shield constructions approved

Use Bludgeoning for Skyvein throws with the ordinary 25% covered-AR bypass on body hits. At the same legal attributes, Light single-target throw Power is **120% of comparable bow Piercing Power** and its range boundaries are **75% of that bow's**. Medium and Heavy use **100% of comparable bow Piercing Power** for one target and **50% of that bow's range boundaries**. Use Shortbow, Recurve, and Longbow as the respective ordinary bow benchmarks for the three classes. The existing 75% per target for two and 55% per target for three apply to the appropriate single-target throw Power. Existing 1/2/3 target caps, independent hit resolution, return, and full-turn loss of shield benefits apply. Exact ordinary bow range distances and detailed return-path rules remain unresolved.

The approved starting full-draw Power benchmarks for **Shortbow / Recurve / Longbow** are **702 / 1,485 / 2,681 Piercing** and **1,048 / 2,218 / 4,005 Slashing** (nearest whole values from the calibration). The corresponding draw caps used are **22 / 32 / 43**. Use the existing quadratic partial-draw rule and ordinary arrowhead bypass. These are working Power benchmarks; ordinary bow range distances remain unresolved.

Approved shield constructions are **Trufula frame with a load-bearing Boughsteel face** (physical Rating ×1.00, support STR ×0.85, with existing applicable Trufula hazards) and **Boughsteel frame with a load-bearing Glassweave face** (Balanced B, including first-physical-wound shatter). A **Nullporcelain inset on a load-bearing Boughsteel face** remains an open design question for magical interception. Boughsteel governs its physical contact. Celestite retains its Quality V triune-forging requirement. Detailed fabrication specifications and hours remain open.

These benchmarks supersede the pending status in earlier Skyvein trials. Files updated are Shield Profiles, Ranged Catalogue, Canon Changelog, and Canon Index.

## Shield spell interception and Skyvein bow benchmark — November 13, 2026

A usable, qualified Nullporcelain or Glassweave shield in Guard can intercept **any incoming spell effect against its bearer**, including psychic effects and the bearer's exposure to an area spell. Resolve the shield's absorption against that exposure. When the shield absorbs the entire incoming spell Power, the bearer is unaffected. When spell Power exceeds what the shield can absorb, the excess reaches the bearer and the spell resolves against them under its normal rules. An area interception protects only that bearer; the area and its other targets resolve normally. If Guard is unavailable under existing rules, including net Extreme Pressure of at least 3 PP, the spell resolves against the bearer normally. Against two genuine coordinated simultaneous flankers, the existing one-interception limit applies; the unblocked attack resolves normally.

Spell magnitude-to-Power conversion, the exact absorption and overflow calculation, partial-effect adjudication for non-damage spells, and whether magical contact causes ceramic wounds remain unresolved.

**Approved balance target:** Skyvein throws should be comparable in effectiveness to a bow with similar stat requirements, accounting for the ability to hit distinct targets and for losing all shield benefits on the throwing turn. Exact throwing Power, range bands, and return-path details remain proposals until selected. The [shield rules and draft trials](29_Physical_Shield_Profiles.md) own the details.

This supersedes the earlier direct-single-target-only interception rule. Updated Shield Profiles, Combat and Shimmer Guard, Ranged Weapon Catalogue, Canon Changelog, and Canon Index.

**Reprise Bronze:** Calculate one Rating at each Quality using `round_half_up(Boughsteel Medium shield Rating × Reprise Bronze Medium armor AR / Boughsteel Medium armor AR)` with all inputs at that Quality. Quality I–V Ratings are **19/33/53/81/112**, fixed across forms. Select a prepared **Light, Medium, or Heavy** form at the start of the wielder's turn without an action. The form lasts until their next turn and governs handling, Guard obstruction, and class-based attack options, including Heavy's Double Strike restriction. Quality and installed enchantments persist. All-form forging remains unresolved, and support STR ×1.00 remains a conditional engineering reference.

Balanced B applies to legal load-bearing ceramics. **Glassweave** uses **×1.25 physical Rating, ×0.95 support STR, ×1.75 magical Rating**. **Nullporcelain** uses **×1.15 physical Rating, ×0.75 support STR, ×3 magical Rating**. Apply the magical multiplier to Rating before squaring for eligible Guard contacts. First-physical-wound shatter and breaking-blow overflow still apply.

Ready **Bellcopper** multiplies final physical shield Defense by **×1.50 Medium / ×2 Heavy**. Actual condition loss after enhanced Defense charges the reservoir, disabling the multiplier until **three uninterrupted qualifying quiet turns** pass. Light shield contact is acoustically muffled. **Hearthiron** Light/Medium/Heavy bash Fire-effect budgets are **10%/20%/35%** of ordinary final bash Power. **Thornspring** holds **one Springload**, which can be spent on a melee block for **one opposing PP for one turn**, or on a bash for **+10% otherwise final bash Power**.

Open rules include magical spell eligibility and Power matching, whether magic can wound ceramic shields, Skyvein range and throwing Power, Bellcopper acoustic scope and qualifying quiet-turn criteria, Hearthiron elemental conversion and heat economy, Thornspring winding, recharge and Pressure refresh, Celestite weapon Leydrain radius and cutoff, and special-material construction, sourcing, and shield fabrication hours.

## November 13, 2026 — Ceramic first-wound shatter; Junk two-state 90% Defense; automatic Guard; qualified half-time smith repair APPROVED (LATEST)

**Latest author explicit revisions supersede the earlier Work-shield report where inconsistent.** **Ceramic load-bearing shields** must be highly defensive for their effective STR requirement but **shatter on the FIRST qualifying physical wound**. Operational contact threshold `P≥D`, where `D=Shield Rating²`, now triggers immediate shattering with no Dented/Cracked ceramic stage. P<D doesn't wound; existing `max(0,P−3D)` only-on-breaking shield torso overflow still applies. This **REPLACES** the older 0.75D/1.75D multi-loss shatter bands from the report. The physical ceramic defense-versus-STR target is approved, but **NO new Nullporcelain or Glassweave shield Rating/STR numbers** were provided; the former optional Nullporcelain ×0.35 and Glassweave ×1.00 Rating references are not satisfactory final ceramic calibration and await author-reviewed alternatives. Keep ceramic BODY ARMOR's own approved wound-severity shatter procedure separate.

**Junk QI Boughsteel shields:** only **two usable conditions** `Intact→Dented→Broken`, rather than ordinary `Intact→Dented→Cracked→Broken`. Junk Shield **Defense Power is exactly 90%** of the matching ordinary QI Boughsteel Shield Defense `Rating²`, NOT 90% of Rating. Use normal 0/1/2/3 shield contact loss bands evaluated on that reduced Defense and cap the loss at Junk's two-loss capacity, applying original only-on-break residual `max(0,P−remaining_Junk_losses×D_Junk)`. General approved Junk costs half matching QI: Light shield 7.5 Gems, Medium/Heavy15 Gems; no unwarranted shield-specific Junk weapon/armor hit-category debuff is invented.

**Guard auto-blocks legal physical hits:** While a genuinely usable shield is in Guard and defender is below **Extreme Pressure net3 PP**, otherwise successful **physically interceptable melee/ranged attacks automatically go to the shield** with no separate block roll, awareness/reflex/reactive-timing or ordinary facing bookkeeping. The combat attack itself must still be a valid hit. This overrides prior routine shield angle-selection, manual interception and precise-projectile timing limitations. A pair of actually **flanking attackers with adjacent initiative places may choose simultaneous attacks**; defender automatically guards exactly one selected threat and the other resolves normally against intended body defenses, not as a free hit. Previously approved voluntary delay for synchronized coordinated attacks remains available. Actual Deflect and Light/Medium Double Strike explicitly surrender active blocks; Heavy shields cannot Double Strike. Guard obstruction +0/+1/+1 remains conditionally applicable only without double counting on the very same shield-contact defense. Extreme Pressure retains its existing restriction; actual incidental collisions with shield are still physical.

**Interim all-equipment smith repair:** A smith able to craft the very item may repair a recoverable/damaged physical object for **HALF that item's lawful complete manufacturing time** and restore its usable condition. Known ordinary weapon repair Light/Medium/Heavy4/8/12h, armor16/20/28h. Standard shield manufacturing time was not ratified; its absolute repair hours await that crafting decision. Repair expense, materials, workforce/market price, salvage and related services are explicitly moved to **MUNDANE CRAFTING AND ECONOMY** backlog. **Ammunition cannot be repaired, except actual reusable throwing weapons**. Existing ordinary ammo forging batches and storage remain unchanged.

**Future Proficiency/verification scope:** Called shots aimed specifically at hands, shield straps and equipment weak points are for future **Proficiency-system** design, not a free current targeted attack; existing exposed-body/armor-gap precision canon remains. End-to-end realistic combat probabilities and fully integrated balance audit are **DEFERRED UNTIL AFTER ENCHANTMENT DESIGN**, which may then be used as an explicitly approved balance lever if needed. Conditional equipment/impact simulations remain historical evidence; no random hit odds or new enchantment parameters approved.

**Special material review:** Work's appendix provided mostly defensive Shield Rating/STR multipliers, NOT shield-specific Skyvein wings, Reprise Bronze form shift, Bellcopper resonance, Hearthiron heat, Thornspring Springload, Oathsilver oath attunement, Nullporcelain/Glassweave comprehensive MR, or Celestite Leydrain/Soul Shred. All suit-only material special powers remain bound to their proper construction. Designing appropriate unique shield versions remains a future author decision, not retroactively approved by the test table. The full detailed new rules and status boundaries are in `29_Physical_Shield_Profiles.md`.

Worn armor, race stats, initiative, existing Combat Speed, other weapon Fs and special material manufacture limitations unchanged.

## November 13, 2026 — Double Strike 60%, shield bash F1.05 and Guard/Deflect/Double Strike APPROVED (LATEST)

**Latest explicit approval:** User says the entire preceding Double Strike/shield combat recommendation is “perfect. Approved.” This **canonizes** the selected 60% final physical Power for EACH of two independently resolved, actually qualified main/offhand attacks within ONE action; one legal target per hand, same opponent or two separate reachable foes, without multiplicative double Sweep/Wide Sweep/Line. The maneuver forfeits normal offhand **Attack +1 credible PP** and normal **Defense counter-pressure** mode, and causes exactly **one self-imposed Pressure Point** from declaration **until start of the user's next turn**. Apply real existing PP tier effects, not automatic hit odds, bonus actions or twice the same Pressure. Weapon-specific scaling, F, material, Quality, valid enchantment and actual damage form/penetration belong to EACH weapon's own separate hit.

**User's crucial clarification:** The intended previous offhand 'dagger problem' meant **no incentive to invest in expensive offhand quality/material/enchantment under the old abstract Attack/Defense tactical choices**. A cheap QI dagger and premium high-end offhand were almost equivalent when only furnishing the PP Attack/Defense role, aside from being able to use the weapon's distinct attack form. **It does not mean that a dagger was too strong in a normal separate attack or that daggers should be banned or penalized.** Approved Double Strike creates an optional real hit that makes the second weapon's physical and properly installed magical specifications valuable. Normal offhand Attack/Defense is preserved as an alternative.

## November 12, 2026 — Physical forge time, Anvilcant crew assistance, END workday, Shimmer weapon/arrow capacity APPROVED (LATEST)

**Express author approval and new directives:** The author approves the preceding STR/STR+DEX/DEX armor-tradeoff analysis and says not to adjust the currently approved damage formula on that evidence. The author separately **approves a new concrete physical forging and Shimmer storage framework**.

**Inventory:** One personal weapon occupies **one Shimmer storage inventory slot**; approximately **30 ordinary arrows** (30 normal single-arrow attacks) fit in **another**. This respects the prior six free Shimmer slots and their upgrades, and must NOT be confused with the eleven distinct equipped-gear positions. Existing large nonpersonal object limits, and non-arrow ammo stack sizes, are not overwritten.

**Forge:** Crafting requires a **dedicated real forge** or **magical portable forge item**. Base 8-hour workdays: Light/Medium/Heavy weapons **1/2/3** days (**8/16/24** hours), Light/Medium/Heavy armor **4/5/7** days (**32/40/56** hours), ammunition **up to 120 pieces in one 8-hour batch**. Anvilcant-trained assistance reduces required work hours **25% for one assistant** or **50% for three**; these are not additive. For every **complete 25 END**, the worker can extend daily work by one hour beyond 8, capped at **16 hours/day**. Shorter workdays provide less project progress and therefore stretch calendar completion. Actual production must still qualify under existing crafting, material, Quality and rare Celestite provisions.

**Operational calculation:** total project labor = listed base hours × relevant approved assistant factor (.75 for 1, .50 for 3, otherwise full baseline where no assistance applies); workday upper limit = min(16, 8 + floor(END/25)); carry partial work hours across days. No invented bonus for exactly two assistants or additional beyond three, no free magical portable forge, no new rank gates, crafting costs, magical equipment effects, exotic ammunition recipes or temporary-stat exceptions.

STR leads in **8/11, 8/11, 9/11, 9/11, 9/11, 9/11**; DEX exceeds the hybrid in **2/11, 3/11, 7/11, 8/11, 8/11, 8/11**. **Drider neutral-STR/DEX example at L100:** STR Greataxe **129,773**, hybrid Zweihander **64,897**, DEX Sabre **74,284**, i.e. actual **STR > DEX > hybrid**. ## November 12, 2026 — Author-conditioned secondary blade-tip Piercing Power reduction APPROVED; greatsword/maul/pike geometry battery

**Latest explicit author direction:** Carry out varied open combat, corridor, formation, reach, armor and defensive-stat tests on greatsword versus maul versus pike. **Only if** secondary Piercing appeared disproportionately capable, reduce its **Power without changing armor penetration**, targeting greatsword secondary Impact **approximately 1.6** in the existing class/shape comparison and about midway between the broad Slashing strike and dedicated Piercing. Tests found that working L20 greatsword secondary **1.707** Impact was **too close** to the dedicated pike's **1.798** despite the greatsword's additional Wide Sweep option (its Slash **1.408**) in the representative B-attack versus E-defense/QII Full Medium AR52 contest. Not a universal proven greatsword overpowered verdict, but enough *role overlap* to justify the author-conditionally authorized modest correction.

**NEW APPROVED BLADE-TIP RULE:** Replace the November11 specific **secondary blade-tip Piercing ×0.82 of its already-adjusted primary F** with **×0.80** (64% primary raw Power rather than 67.24%; a **~4.82%** reduction from previous secondary raw Power), applied **once**. The tested greatsword thrust yields **Impact1.624** in the same designated reference, very close to target 1.6 and between Slash1.408 and pike1.798. An exact 1.6 would require ×~0.794, rejected as needless precision for this balance purpose. No other specific Power multiplier change is authorized.

**UNCHANGED:** All legitimate ordinary primary/secondary Piercing retain **50% covered Armor Resistance bypass**; earned actual rear-hit improvement **+10 percentage points** remains; purpose-built secondary **spike/beak ×0.90** remains, as does the general applicable other-secondary ×0.90 default, original greatsword shape ×0.875, pike dedicated shape ×0.90, Bludgeoning/Slashing/primary Piercing forms, armor AR, STR/DEX/END/SPD, Shimmer Guard, class/movement/accuracy rules, material factors, hit probabilities not designed, real geometry and item purchase prices. No blade obtains a Point thrust without a mechanically plausible tip. Do not multiply draft full weapon F by already-incorporated class/shape factors.

**Full battle battery:** Screening every level1–20 with STR+DEX B attacker vs S/E/B defenders, Quality I→II Light/Medium/Heavy where stat eligible yields **81 legal reference encounters**, with **all 81 reduced raw conditional Impact**, **4** losing one injury stage (L18 S/B QII Medium from 3→2; L20 S/B QII Heavy from 2→1). **Not an accuracy or victory-rate statistic.** At L20 END43/QII Medium, ratios are **GS Slashing1.408**, **old GS thrust1.707**, **new GS thrust1.624**, **pike Piercing1.798**, **maul Blunt1.639**. Against QII Heavy, **0.706/1.179→1.122/1.242/0.934** respectively; the slash has less armor penetration, while new Point is still useful. Actual earned rear attacks, exposed/joint weakpoints, broader L10/L16/L25/L50 cases and Heavy Adamantite versus Boughsteel sensitivities were tested. Special purpose beaks/spikes in draft Medium weapon shapes land at **~81–82.4% of dedicated Piercing Power** versus comparable purpose-built war pick, so they did **not** require a blanket reduction.

**Battlefield role outcomes:** Open arc of three accessible frontal foes, sufficient swing clearance: greatsword and maul Wide Sweep up to three (squad-only aggregate ×2); pike Line only one unless aligned. Tight corridor with three unobstructed depth-aligned targets: greatsword primary Wide Sweep and maul Wide Sweep are **not legal due clearance**, greatsword Point may threaten one, pike Line can threaten up to three **only when each is physically accessible and unblocked**. Shield or front obstruction limits line access; no penetration or aggregate benefit from a blocked target. A real established Short grapple inside Long reach defeats both greatsword and pike ordinary Long strikes; maul's Medium reach is case-dependent, not automatically effective. Long-vs-Short defender SPD ratios **1.25/1.50** still control harder/unsupported approach opportunities, with pressure exceptions and real armor mobility burdens. No new attack actions, individual-target Power multiplication or hit probabilities.

**CRITICAL individual-F qualifier:** The F1.395625 greatsword Slash and F1.1165 new Point are **working class/form/shape normalization**, NOT acceptance of the old draft **whole-item F1.27**. If that different unapproved single total F1.27 were selected, its new secondary F would be **1.016** and the example Impact **~1.345**, illustrating that the precise 1.624 target is reference-specific, not universal. Full individual Fs, handling requirements and final weapon catalog balancing remain open; the modest ×0.80 blade-tip rule is the approved global exception. Long-term actual win rates cannot be inferred without an approved evasion success system.

**Files updated directly to main:** `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md` (comprehensive test and operative rule), `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md` (operative combat rule), `25_Melee_Weapon_Catalogue_DRAFT.md` (shared rule and eight rederived **still-unapproved** individual draft secondary F displays), this changelog and `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md` (latest authority pointer). ## November 12, 2026 — Three-path physical equipment balance tests recorded (EXPLORATORY; no new rule approval)

**Author direction:** The author approved continuing with all three proposed balancing paths: (1) physical weapon forms and secondary Piercing, (2) armor Quality versus protective class, and (3) STR/SPD, STR/END and STR/DEX character investment. This is **approval to test and document findings**, not approval of any new F, AR, accuracy distribution, equipment price or progression requirement.

**Governing supersession respected:** Already-approved genuine primary AND secondary Piercing uses **50% covered-AR bypass**. Blade-tip secondary **×0.82 of adjusted primary F**, purpose-built spike/beak **×0.90**. Greatsword shape adjustment **×0.875** and pike primary shape factor **×0.90** apply once. Older greatsword thrust ×0.90/25%-AR-bypass and specialized 65% Piercing were NOT reinstated. All absolute item F values remain calibrated working references pending individual author approval.

**Test findings (detailed reproducible setup in `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md`):**
- **Attack forms:** At common Medium-reference F, a generic blade-tip thrust derived from Slashing generates **~0.44% more conditional landed raw Power** than a same-class shape-neutral dedicated Piercing reference, and shares its 50% AR bypass. This is a **WATCH** for universal near-equivalence, not a new license for unqualified weapons to thrust. In shape-aware Heavy test at L20, pike primary F1.1745 yields only **~5.3% more same-A Power** than a greatsword thrust F1.1444125; versus END43/QII Boughsteel Medium armor, pike Impact≈1.80/stage2, greatsword thrust≈1.71/stage1. Wider tactical value and item-specific tuning still matter.
- **Armor:** Across 20 levels and four STR/SPD versus STR/END pairing cases with eligibility enforced, injury-stage reductions were **Light QI→QII: 8/80**, **Medium QI→QII: 18/72**, **Heavy QI→QII: 8/20**, **Light QI→Medium QI: 44/72**, **Medium QI→Heavy QI: 18/20**. Category changes from material/class SPD penalties were also checked; armor class improvement is potent but can ease incoming hit difficulty. Counts are *deterministic scenarios, not hit odds*.
- **Investment:** At L16 both in QII Medium with Medium blunt reference, STR/SPD attacking STR/END is **Easy, 1 injury conditional**, while reverse is **Very Hard, 1 injury conditional**. In QI Light, reverse can deliver **3 injuries** if it actually connects. At L20 STR/DEX Both governing A≈57.3625 versus one-stat STR51.25, but SPD19 versus fast build SPD38; the stronger dual-stat attacks remain harder to land against the fast build.

**Judgment:** Keep approved global weapon-form, Junk, armor, attribute, Guard and hit-category rules unchanged. Potential **greatsword versatility versus pike dedicated-Piercing distinctiveness** deserves targeted individual-F/geometry checks; Quality/class armor investment and SPD/END provide real conditional tradeoffs. **Unresolved:** actual hit percentages, outcomes/durations, individual item Fs/minima, offhand/shield interference, extended materials/species, magic, costs and specific weapon eligibility. No new simulator-dice system or probability claim introduced.

**Files:** `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md` holds full test method and tabulations; this changelog records exploratory status; `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md` points to findings.

## November 12, 2026 — Fractional Junk accessory bonuses final-floor APPROVED; levels 1–20 two-track combat tests

**Latest explicit author approval:** For Junk QI accessories, their **halved numerical attribute bonuses** are allowed to contribute real fractional **+0.5 stat points**; **add all separately legal equipped accessory contributions affecting the SAME stat before rounding the final affected stat DOWN ONCE**. Example: two +0.5 accessories give +1; three +0.5 accessories give +1.5, so an otherwise integer stat20 becomes21. Do NOT floor each individual +0.5 early, round every item up, pool bonuses between unrelated stats, create half sockets, or invent extra Soul Strain reductions. Original Centaur half-bonus and item-level racial rounding remain a **specific exception to preserve**; full mixed-affinity rounding ordering for multiple accessory groups is a future edge-case check. No general global change to unrelated fractional racial effective attributes was approved by this Junk accessories-only discussion. **Actual enchant-slot capacities, odd-number and nonstat enhancement mechanics remain open.**

**Combat test user request fulfilled:** Run two levels **1 through 20** sets: **A normal-equipped enemies** (ordinary QI weapon and armor from first level, QII weapon at level16) and **B mirrored-upgrade enemies** (both start Junk and upgrade when Hero does). Test Hero chosen replacement phases **L1–5 Junk weapon+armor**, **L6–10 normal QI weapon/Junk armor**, **L11–15 normal QI weapon+armor**, **L16–20 normal QII weapon/QI armor**. Full equipment and purchase schedules are *testing choices*, not compulsory progression. Each of **20 levels × 2 tracks × 2 Hero stat allocations × 4 enemy SPD/END profiles = 320 deterministic encounter states** was checked. Hero exemplar is a canon Thornguard with a **working F1.15 Medium mace-like Bludgeoning Narrow** attack and QI Boughsteel Full Light AR25; melee individual-weapon F remains draft and QII raw output is held at same reference F to avoid inventing a new Power coefficient. No probability/dice, hit-rate or actual guaranteed victories are claimed: existing six-category attack ladder does not have numeric hit probabilities.

**Peer matchup results, Hero-outgoing/incoming difficulty:** L1–5 normal-enemy **Hard/Easy** versus mirror **Average/Average**; L6–10 normal **Average/Easy** versus mirror **Easy/Easy**; L11–20 both **Average/Average**. Thus early Junk **versus Junk cancels**, normal foes punish un-upgraded player, and simultaneous weapon upgrades with both still in Junk armor make both parties easier to hit for five levels. One fast foe (SPD×1.30) at level1 with normal equipment gives **Very Hard/Certain**, against mirrored Junk **Hard/Easy**. Extreme speedy foe (SPD×1.60) versus starting Junk player is **Impossible/Certain** when normally equipped, but **Very Hard/Easy** if also in Junk. Difficult combat must allow existing terrain, pressure, alternate damage and withdrawal; these are synthetic high-threat examples, not auto-win/lose dice predictions.

**Impact/Guard sensitivity:** Working F1.15 STR-led blunt strike, 25% physical AR bypass, QI Boughsteel Full Light AR25, and the latest post-rebase quadratic Power/END²+AR² yield fresh equal-gear Strength/Speed investment **Solid hit stage1 at levels1–7**, **Devastating stage2 at8–15**, **Overwhelming stage3 at16–20** when armor stays QI Light. With STR/END investment instead, matching level1–20 peers take only **Solid** initial landed hits under this exact example. Heroes retain five Shimmer Guard injury advancements and ordinary foes have three; a one-landed Overwhelming wound from around level16 can defeat the ordinary foe but cannot incapacitate a fresh Hero without separately authorized exceptions. **This observation is stat-allocation and frozen-low-quality armor dependent**, not reason to change already approved physical armor F/AR, global Junk modifiers or natural END. An additional level1 END×1.25 and SPD×0.75 bruiser produces a Player Impact Ratio **~0.69 Superficial** while the return is **~0.89 Solid**: in a hypothetical all-hit attrition stress sequence the Hero cannot wound this opponent before losing. No actual stochastic combat win rate is possible from current canon.

**Result/recommendations:** Retain approved Junk penalties unchanged. The cost/accuracy tradeoffs are promising, particularly the starter-to-normal upgrade. **Monitor the vulnerable weapon-first / Junk-armor interval**, and in later test compare light armor QI→QII or better, and tactical alternative to inappropriate high-END brute-force encounters. Formal accuracy-percentage statistics and actual durations are not approved. **Tests and limits are documented in `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md`; no new tactical probabilities or enemy templates are canon.** `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md` already owns the six-category implementation; no new combat rules were added.

**Files updated in this approval/test round:** `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md`, `10_Canon_Changelog.md`, `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md`. Starting Junk grants, gem/Glint budget, conditional 50% shop buyback, 30%-of-lifetime Gem consumables, material-neutral pricing and Celestite prohibitions remain unchanged.

## November 12, 2026 — Junk equipment handling penalty, half enchant capacity and starter gear approved; first tests

**Latest user explicit approval (supersedes older "Junk drawback numerics unresolved" records):** The already-approved Junk condition costs **50%** of the comparable ordinary **Quality I, Boughsteel-based** same-form equipment. A Junk weapon's **attacks are one hit-difficulty CATEGORY HARDER for the wielder to land**; Junk armor makes **ordinary evasion-resolved attacks against its wearer one category EASIER for the attacker to land**. These are shifts on the existing Certain/Easy/Average/Hard/Very Hard/Impossible six-category ladder; apply each relevant Junk role once per attack, so Junk weapon versus Junk armor nets zero; do not stack multiple worn Junk subpieces for repeated penalties. Keep normal categorical endpoints and all genuine attack-validity requirements. **Do not reduce weapon F/Power, armor AR/MR, physical STR/DEX/SPD/END, cause new automatic breakage, add a new percentage evasion system or grant extra attack actions.** The new rule is concrete even if the exact hit-probability algorithm remains intentionally narrative.

**Accessories and future magical implements:** A Junk accessory has **50% of ordinary Quality I bonuses AND 50% ordinary QI enchantment potential**. Future Junk implements should follow the same principle, but **implement mechanics are intentionally not designed yet**. Rounding half of odd-number numerical effects, fractional socket/charge capacity and non-numeric properties are unresolved; no invented half socket, new Soul Strain discount, free magic or forced stat floor. Junk shields and special blocking interactions still await normal shield-form adjudication.

**New starting-character rule APPROVED:** A starting Hero receives **one eligible Junk weapon and one Junk armor ensemble** as **starting equipment**, tailored to anatomy and ordinary physical usability. They are granted items, **NOT extra cash, Gem Shop purchased merchandise or free 50% resale eligibility**. **Explicit author correction:** starter item value **may exceed W(1)=30 Gems**, which is a reference planning target, NOT a hard cap for initial gifted items. No mandatory balancing payout to other Heroes, no forced deduced Gem wallet, and no change to W10=200/W25=400 and later tier wealth targets. The free starter junk pair's appraisal does not imply the Hero has enough liquid Gems to immediately replace it.

**Small focused tier tests, not new catalogue tariffs:** Assume *illustrative category* standard QI primary 60/armor 40 Gems, Junk 30/20 and all other Junk-support positions 75. At **L1**, given 30+20=**50 Gems** of starting gear, 20 above W1, which is deliberate. At **L10** W200, keeping full Junk pair+support costs **125 Gems**, upgrading just weapon to normal QI → **155**, upgrading just armor to normal QI → **145**, spending 120 on normal QII weapon while retaining 95 in Junk support → **215 Gems**, exceeding W10 by 15 (omit support). At **L25** W400, normal QII weapon plus ordinary QI armor and Junk other support → **235 Gems**; proposed normal QIII primary OR substantively enchanted QII primary 240, Junk armor and Junk other support → **335 Gems**, preserving 65 of budget headroom but poor support gear. These are **total owned-portfolio planning values, not liquid cash**, and magic/enchant effects of Junk accessories cannot be assumed freely available. These results support gradual upgrading versus early primary specialization but do not test real shopping stock, exact magical affixes or character build output.

**Categorical combat tests:** An otherwise Average direct attack becomes **Hard** if made by Junk weapon only, **Easy** if target wears Junk armor only, and returns to **Average** if both apply. From Very Hard, Junk weapon may push to **Impossible**, a balance concern to watch in real play. No armor Defense/physical injury rates or actual probabilistic hit frequencies were altered or simulated.

**Updated owning references:** `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md` (operative Junk rules, starting items, arithmetic tests and limitations); `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md` (combat-category interaction); this changelog and `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md` (approval and supersession). **Outstanding:** accessory half-bonus rounding and magical installation potential, junk shields and unusual forms, exact starting gear form/stocks, real encounter probabilities and equipment-price validation, and later implements. Retired material/price rules stay retired.

## November 12, 2026 — Material-neutral Hero Gems APPROVED; Celestite +20% price retired; impurity purely narrative; focused tests

**Latest explicit author approval, superseding our prior open question:** At matching **equipment design/weapon shape or armor class, coverage, workmanship Quality, and comparable enchantment installation**, **chosen material does not add or subtract any standard Hero Gem-equivalent cost**. Characters specializing in STR/DEX/other stats should not face a second material rarity or power premium just because they invested to meet item requirements. **Material still determines all previously approved Power/AR/MR, weight/handling, mobility costs, vulnerabilities, attunement, special abilities and real physical construction restrictions.** This applies to weapons, armor and other otherwise equivalent forms; don't exempt a special-material device through a disguised cost surcharge. Separately unusual engineered design or independently installed magic can carry their own price. No economic rule silently changes existing mechanics.

**Celestite author-approved price correction:** The immediately previous **1.20× equivalent Adamantite QV armor crafting valuation is NOW SUPERSEDED** (older ×5 historical already retired). New nominal **Celestite QV = ×1.00 comparable Adamantite QV** at same equipment design/class/coverage/workmanship. This is a *Gem-equivalent appraisal*, not a shop sale: **Celestite still QV ONLY**, requiring real material, extraordinary qualified Centaur smith and **simultaneous personal aid of Arrest, Surrender and Baphomet**, and still imposes approved intrinsic MP drain, Leydrain, Soul Shred/XP erosion. No buyer can substitute Gems for divine help or obtain an ordinary vendor-stock Celestite item. Older Celestite-specific material price table and prior 20% record remain as **SUPERSEDED** historical records.

**Author clarification: purity is ONLY an IN-WORLD explanation:** No material purity stat, refinement level, alloy percentage gate, extra item-tier/Quality, bonus penalty to F/AR/MR/handling, or impurity progression is introduced. A future **parallel conventional-currency economy** will separately value bar purity, real quantities and labor; Centaurs can already **craft and enchant without touching divine Gems**. The author's bar example is illustrative: one nearly pure Adamantite bar might provide material for many lightly-alloyed swords, whereas a massive greatsword might consume multiple bars. These are **NOT approved recipes, mass ratios or mundane coin valuations**, and no Gem-to-mortal-currency exchange is declared. All current standard Gem-price references are game-economy planning, not proof that ores are equally expensive in mortal markets.

**Focused tests documented in `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md`:** At STR40 QV Heavy STR-led reference Boughsteel Power ~3639 versus Adamantite ~5685 with the matching one-time ×1.25 material F, **+56.25%** physical Power, while illustrative QV Heavy maul stat minima **STR16 vs STR38**. QV Full Heavy Boughsteel **AR115/STR36/SPD−20%**, Adamantite **AR170/STR91/SPD−30%**, Nullporcelain **AR0/MR170/STR26/SPD−15%**, Glassweave **AR115/MR115/STR35/SPD−19%** but shatter vulnerability; Bellcopper **AR115/STR48/SPD−25%** has only conditional ready ×2 defense; Celestite **AR180/MR185/STR65/SPD−24%** requires triune forging and imposes intrinsic **15 MP/turn** plus **5% of first-donning XP snapshot per voluntarily engaged combat turn**. These preserve strong niche identities and attribute access but **do not prove global game balance**. Adamantite can dominate a qualified weapon comparison absent other nonprice tradeoffs; Bellcopper and Glassweave are situational priorities to test with actual impacts, repairs and spell threats. No weapon/armor stats or penalties were altered.

**Scope and files:** `09_Equipment_and_Economy.md` now owns the pricing rule and test report; `07_Centaurs_and_Smithcraft.md` records independent mundane forging and the Celestite exception; `22_Combat_Endurance_and_Shimmer_Guard.md` records NO combat changes; `10_Canon_Changelog.md` and `00_Mystaria_Canon_Index.md` record canon precedence. **W100=3,200 Gems**, 30%-primary-item pattern, 100 Glints/Gem, 30% of lifetime Gems spent on consumables, conditional Gem Shop 50% buyback, Quality I Boughsteel-only Junk 50% cost, and enchanted item ~×2 price guideline remain unchanged. Exact base class/coverage/form prices, Junk mechanical weakness, specialty crafted forms, enchanting installation price/strain, actual mundane economy, and Celestite sourcing remain unresolved.

## November 12, 2026 — Enchanted Primary Item ×2 and Junk gear accepted; equal-material pricing considered

**Explicit author approval:** Accept the latest proposed early equipment purchasing strategy, with the author's correction that a tier one step above costs **60% of typical portfolio**, but **two steps above 120%**, NOT 60%. Keep normal tier I–V budget milestones **200/400/800/1600/3200 Gems** and typical unenchanted Primary Item targets **60/120/240/480/960 Gems**. The 30% Primary Item is the Hero's single largest deliberate investment, weapon for many or armor/shield for others, **not a surcharge** based on declaration. There is no new use-level requirement.

**Author-approved economic guideline:** A **meaningfully enchanted** item of the same actual Quality, form and functional type should cost **around ×2** the corresponding ordinary nonmagical item; typical primary investments become **120/240/480/960/1920 Gems** when fully enchanted. This is NOT a new physical Quality VI or unrestricted enchant access; Soul Strain, race exceptions, rune and gem eligibility remain as established, with magic effect-specific fees to be developed. Existing **3040-Gem full-slot example** had mixed form/magic cost allocations, so it cannot be simultaneously charged a second full enchantment fee without recomputing; switching its 960-Gem primary to a 1920-Gem one costs **4000 total**, which exceeds W100 by 800 Gems and requires supporting compromises. Tiny utility runes need not double every item automatically.

**Author-approved Junk category:** All Junk equipment is **Quality I, Boughsteel-based**, and costs **half the corresponding standard Quality I same-shape/category item price**. For example, normal QI primary **60 Gems** versus Junk **30 Gems**. Junk is not a new sixth Quality, and has intentionally inferior condition/reliability to make standard QI a dependable upgrade. **Exact combat penalties, repair/breakage, item eligibility, nonmetal accessory implementation and magical compatibility remain unresolved**; not silently equal to QI performance for half cost. At level10 W200, QI primary + ten half-price QI support examples = **155 Gems**, while a QII primary + ten Junk support is **215 Gems**, forcing at least 15 Gems in supporting tradeoffs.

**Equal-cost material policy question currently UNDER REVIEW:** The author suggests that two items of the same design, coverage and Quality should have the same standard Gem cost across materials, because the character already pays attribute/handling tradeoffs (e.g. Adamantite stronger but harder to wield). They further **suggest** removing Celestite's existing +20% Gem valuation for consistency. ## November 11, 2026 — Ranged draw, reload, and opening-hit benchmarks approved

**Bow draw.** For a shot the archer can legally make, usable draw is the lower of effective STR and the engineered draw cap. Shot Power is the bow-and-arrow full-draw Power multiplied by `(usable draw / draw cap)^2`. DEX governs aim and handling. Individual full-draw Power, draw caps, and minimum controllable partial draw remain open for item calibration.

**Reload pace.** Use one reload turn for most handheld profiles in the working comparison and two for the arbalest. A loaded shot takes its normal attack action. Time spent reloading is separate. Ordinary bow nocking and drawing use the existing bow procedure. Preserve the approved full-turn single-shot pistol and high-capacity magazine reloads. Individual capacity, cycling exceptions, and mounted or siege crew cycles remain subject to their own profiles.

**Damage target.** Give slower ranged weapons a stronger opening hit. Tune the stronger first hit and the full firing cycle together against unarmored, Medium-armored, and Heavy-armored targets. Equal sustained injury output is not the design target. This approval establishes the calibration method and pacing, not the menu's individual shot Power, ammunition, range, or mount test values.

Recorded in Equipment and Economy, Combat, the ranged catalogue, and the Canon Index.
